title: 嘉靖四十年浙江武舉鄉試錄
text:
浙江武舉鄉試錄序
我
國家設文武制科網羅豪俊以
共建久安長治之業蓋較然
埒重矣曩歲武科雖間一報
罷旋卽舉行如故且不限額
而申諭加詳焉誠重之也今
年辛酉八月浙江巡按御史
崔公〔棟〕旣大比登儁錄賢書
以獻
===
天子矣乃冬十月當武舉先是崔
公一日集藩臬諸君論兵事
喟然而嘆曰吾聞今有司者
類多具文以應上而武舉特
punctuated:
浙江武舉鄉試錄序

我國家設文武制科，網羅豪俊，以共建久安長治之業，蓋較然埒重矣。曩歲武科雖間一報罷，旋卽舉行如故，且不限額，而申諭加詳焉，誠重之也。今年辛酉八月，浙江巡按御史崔公〔棟〕旣大比登儁，錄賢書以獻天子矣。乃冬十月，當武舉。先是，崔公一日集藩臬諸君，論兵事，喟然而嘆曰：「吾聞今有司者，類多具文以應上，而武舉特
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Zhejiang Military Provincial Examination

Our dynasty established civil and military examinations to gather outstanding men, that together they might build an enduring order of peace and good government. Clearly, the two were accorded equal importance. In earlier years, although the military examination was occasionally suspended, it was soon held again as before. Moreover, no quota was imposed, and reiterated instructions became increasingly detailed. Truly, it was taken seriously.

In the eighth month of this xinyou year [1561], Lord Cui [Dong], Regional Inspector of Zhejiang, had already selected outstanding men through the triennial Provincial Examination and compiled the register of worthy candidates for presentation to the Son of Heaven. Then, in the tenth month, in winter, the military examination fell due. Before this, Lord Cui had one day assembled the officials of the Provincial Administration and Surveillance Commissions to discuss military affairs. He sighed deeply and said: “I hear that officials nowadays mostly prepare perfunctory paperwork to satisfy their superiors, and that in the military examination this is especially …

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江武舉鄉試錄
text:
甚衆是何以來干城之豪仰
塞
明詔哉人言文武代爲雌雄有時
而用此誠隅曲之見欲與圖
治難矣乃下令諸司凡所張
設悉加隆重獎籍一如文科
之制於是諸郡衛武弁暨諸
===
軍民之子聞御史令咸躍然
思奮起囊弓矢裹糧策馬窮
日夜馳至投牒有司視往歲
增什九云至期檄左布政使
胡堯臣右參政杜拯爲提調
副使范惟一劉存德爲監試
其諸執事咸慎選以克既會
punctuated:
甚。衆是何以來干城之豪，仰塞明詔哉？人言文武代爲雌雄，有時而用，此誠隅曲之見，欲與圖治難矣。」乃下令諸司，凡所張設，悉加隆重，獎籍一如文科之制。
於是諸郡衛武弁暨諸軍民之子，聞御史令，咸躍然思奮起，囊弓矢，裹糧策馬，窮日夜馳至，投牒有司，視往歲增什九云。至期，檄左布政使胡堯臣、右參政杜拯爲提調，副使范惟一、劉存德爲監試，其諸執事咸慎選以克。既會
translation_en:
…especially so. How can this [?] attract outstanding men who can serve as our shields and ramparts, and thereby fulfill the illustrious imperial edict? People say that civil and military pursuits alternate in ascendancy, each having its time of usefulness. This is truly a narrow, partial view; it would be difficult to plan good government with such people.” He therefore ordered the various offices to conduct all arrangements with greater solemnity and distinction, and to follow the regulations for the civil examinations in granting recognition and entering names on the rolls [?].
Thereupon, military officers from the various prefectures and guard units, together with sons of military and civilian households, heard the censor’s order and eagerly sought to distinguish themselves. Packing their bows and arrows and wrapping provisions, they mounted their horses and rode day and night to arrive and submit their applications to the authorities. Their numbers reportedly exceeded those of previous years by nine-tenths. When the appointed time came, official dispatches designated Hu Yaochen, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner, and Du Zheng, Right Administration Vice Commissioner, as Proctors, and Fan Weiyi and Liu Cunde, Surveillance Vice Commissioners, as examination monitors. All the other functionaries were carefully selected for their ability to carry out their duties [?]. Having assembled …

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江武舉鄉試錄
text:
諸司以乙丑試騎射戊辰試
步射乃辛未旦日進諸𣪍者
鑰院嚴課之得五十人焉按
故事有錄屬惟一序諸篇端
序曰吾聞聖王之制兵也端
委穆清之上而折衝萬里之
外拱揖指撝而四海賔服者
===
以所擇將得人也昔人謂得
十利劒不若得歐冶之巧得
百走馬不若得伯樂之數何
者干將莫邪之利惟歐冶能
神其割而騕褭飛兔稱良於
天下非伯樂無以善其材矧
夫王者挈封疆之重總師徒
punctuated:
諸司以乙丑試騎射，戊辰試步射，乃辛未旦日進諸𣪍者，鑰院嚴課之，得五十人焉。按故事有錄，屬惟一序諸篇端。
序曰：吾聞聖王之制兵也，端委穆清之上，而折衝萬里之外；拱揖指撝，而四海賔服者，以所擇將得人也。昔人謂：「得十利劒，不若得歐冶之巧；得百走馬，不若得伯樂之數。」何者？干將、莫邪之利，惟歐冶能神其割；而騕褭、飛兔稱良於天下，非伯樂無以善其材。矧夫王者挈封疆之重，總師徒
translation_en:
…the various offices conducted the mounted archery test on the yichou day and the archery test on foot on the wuchen day. Then, at dawn on the xinwei day, they admitted those who had qualified [?], locked the examination compound, and examined them rigorously, selecting fifty men. Following precedent, a record was compiled, and Weiyi was charged with writing a preface to stand at its beginning.
The preface reads: I have heard that when sage kings organized their military forces, they wore ceremonial robes in the serene heights of their court, yet repelled aggression ten thousand li away. With folded hands, courteous gestures, and the pointing of a finger, they brought all within the four seas into willing submission. This was because they chose the right men as generals. The ancients said: “Obtaining ten sharp swords is not as good as obtaining the craftsmanship of Ouye; obtaining a hundred swift horses is not as good as obtaining the discernment of Bole.” Why is this? Sharp though Ganjiang and Moye were, only Ouye could make their cutting power wondrous. And though Yaoniao and Feitu were renowned throughout the realm as excellent horses, without Bole there was no means of bringing their abilities to full use. How much more does this apply when a king shoulders the weighty responsibility for his frontiers and commands his armies…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江武舉鄉試錄
text:
之衆而付諸其人豈直利劒
走馬等哉故自昔王者重閫
外之寄每命將則必卜吉受
鼓旗親操斧鉞授將以柄而
頮歲以來我
皇上允注情邊疆數降詔求將皇
皇如不及又豈直欲得歐冶
===
伯樂其人哉然吾聞之蜚景
之劒運掌不留行以之封穫
則歐冶袖手而郤步千里之
馬以服鹽車則伯樂聵目而
不眡故夫王者之求將必誠
重之而後將可得也乃今
聖天子求將甚急而御史將順德
punctuated:
之衆而付諸其人，豈直利劒、走馬等哉？故自昔王者重閫外之寄，每命將則必卜吉，受鼓旗，親操斧鉞，授將以柄。而頮歲以來，我皇上允注情邊疆，數降詔求將，皇皇如不及，又豈直欲得歐冶、伯樂其人哉？
然吾聞之，蜚景之劒，運掌不留行；以之封穫，則歐冶袖手而郤步。千里之馬，以服鹽車，則伯樂聵目而不眡。故夫王者之求將，必誠重之，而後將可得也。乃今聖天子求將甚急，而御史將順德
translation_en:
…the multitude of his troops and entrust them to such a man—could this be merely comparable to sharp swords and swift horses? Thus, from antiquity, kings have attached great importance to commands beyond the palace gates. Whenever appointing a general, they would divine an auspicious day, bestow drums and banners [?], personally take up the battle-axe, and give the general its handle. In recent years [?], our Emperor has truly devoted his attention to the frontiers, repeatedly issuing edicts seeking generals, with an urgency as though he could never find them soon enough. Surely he seeks more than merely men like Ou Ye and Bo Le?
Yet I have heard that the sword Feijing, wielded in the hand, cuts through without impediment; but use it for harvesting [?], and Ou Ye would fold his hands into his sleeves and step back. Harness a horse capable of travelling a thousand li to a salt cart, and Bo Le would close his eyes [?] and refuse to look. Thus, when a king seeks generals, he must sincerely value them; only then can generals be obtained. Now the sagely Son of Heaven seeks generals with the utmost urgency, and the censor, furthering his virtuous…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江武舉鄉試錄
text:
美舉行又特隆是誠古推轂
之遺也以今觀諸士在收者
精騎射熟韜鈐善批擣之術
達五官之用將固人人能矣
然皆佐勝之具也非所以必
勝也吾請以古上將之道告
焉古者將之受君命也對曰
===
二心不可以事君疑志不可
以應敵臣既受制於前願君
垂一言之命於臣也君許之
乃乘將軍車載旗鼓斧鉞而
行其臨敵決勝無天於上無
地於下無敵於前無有二心
斯之謂上將而必勝之道也
punctuated:
美，舉行又特隆，是誠古推轂之遺也。以今觀諸士，在收者精騎射，熟韜鈐，善批擣之術，達五官之用，將固人人能矣。然皆佐勝之具也，非所以必勝也。吾請以古上將之道告焉。
古者將之受君命也，對曰：「二心不可以事君，疑志不可以應敵。臣既受制於前，願君垂一言之命於臣也。」君許之，乃乘將軍車，載旗鼓斧鉞而行。其臨敵決勝，無天於上，無地於下，無敵於前，無有二心，斯之謂上將而必勝之道也。
translation_en:
…virtue, and the conduct of this examination has been especially grand. This truly preserves the ancient practice of pushing forward a general’s carriage when sending him into command. Looking now at these candidates, those selected are proficient in mounted archery, well versed in military strategy, skilled in methods of striking and assaulting, and conversant with the functions of the five officers [?]. Certainly, every one of them is capable of serving as a general. Yet these are all means of assisting victory, not means of ensuring it. Allow me to tell them of the way of the supreme commanders of antiquity.
In ancient times, when a general received his sovereign’s command, he replied: “With divided loyalties one cannot serve one’s sovereign; with an uncertain resolve one cannot confront the enemy. Having received your orders in your presence, your servant asks that you bestow a single command upon him.” The sovereign granted this request. The general then mounted the commander’s carriage and departed with banners, drums, and battle-axes. When confronting the enemy and deciding the victory, he acknowledged no Heaven above, no Earth below, and no enemy before him; he harbored no divided purpose. This is what is called the way of the supreme commander, the way that ensures victory.

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江武舉鄉試錄
text:
諸士能無意乎吾又聞之昔
人不愛尺壁而愛寸陰以時
難遭而易失也故良將之趨
時也衣不解帶屨遺不躡所
以乘遇合而樹勲伐也諸士
踴躍而來志厲青雲氣如飄
風壯矣壯矣且復幸遇
===
聖明在上竝用文武而御史與諸
大夫方覆虛左之懷崇鷹揚
之典此誠千載一時也行矣
寧不慷慨奮策爲
國家揚威四遠哉是舉也督撫
尚書胡公宗憲弘猷振武士
爭淬厲巡鹽御史袁公淳飭
punctuated:
諸士能無意乎？吾又聞之：昔人不愛尺壁而愛寸陰，以時難遭而易失也。故良將之趨時也，衣不解帶，屨遺不躡，所以乘遇合而樹勲伐也。諸士踴躍而來，志厲青雲，氣如飄風，壯矣！壯矣！且復幸遇聖明在上，竝用文武，而御史與諸大夫方覆虛左之懷，崇鷹揚之典，此誠千載一時也。行矣，寧不慷慨奮策，爲國家揚威四遠哉！
是舉也，督撫尚書胡公宗憲弘猷振武，士爭淬厲；巡鹽御史袁公淳飭
translation_en:
Can you gentlemen fail to take this to heart? I have also heard that men of old prized not a foot-wide jade disk but an inch of time, because the right moment is hard to encounter and easily lost. Thus, when a good general hastens to seize an opportunity, he does not loosen the belt of his robes; if a shoe falls off, he does not stop to put it back on. In this way he takes advantage of a favorable encounter and establishes meritorious achievements. You gentlemen have come eagerly, your aspirations reaching to the blue clouds and your spirit like a whirlwind. Magnificent! Magnificent! Moreover, you are fortunate to encounter a sage and enlightened ruler on the throne, employing both civil and military talent. The censor and the other officials now cherish the intention of reserving the place of honor for worthy men [?] and exalt the institution for selecting martial talent, those who “soar like eagles.” This truly is an opportunity that comes once in a thousand years. Go forth! How could you fail to rouse yourselves with ardor and wield the whip, spreading the state's martial prestige to the farthest reaches?
For this examination, Minister Hu Zongxian, serving as supreme commander and grand coordinator, has invigorated military affairs through his grand designs, and the candidates vie to temper and sharpen themselves. The Salt-inspecting Censor, Yuan Chun, has set in order …

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江武舉鄉試錄
text:
紀宣威風聲表著刑部郎中
林君烶章工部主事馮君符
南京戶部主事黎君元谷以
使事至右布政使徐南金左
叅議唐愛右叅議于錦副使
凌雲翼李燧李僑王春澤宋
守志僉事歸大道唐堯臣徐
===
栻陳宗虞署都指揮僉事鄭
維清王灝咸從事於外共董
厥成左叅政谷中虛僉事曹
天祐署都指揮僉事管海先
以
表賀行始事協謀均有勞焉如
例益書之
punctuated: 紀宣威，風聲表著。刑部郎中林君烶章、工部主事馮君符、南京戶部主事黎君元谷，以使事至。右布政使徐南金、左叅議唐愛、右叅議于錦、副使凌雲翼、李燧、李僑、王春澤、宋守志、僉事歸大道、唐堯臣、徐栻、陳宗虞、署都指揮僉事鄭維清、王灝，咸從事於外，共董厥成。左叅政谷中虛、僉事曹天祐、署都指揮僉事管海，先以表賀行，始事協謀，均有勞焉。如例益書之。
translation_en: …discipline and displayed authority, making his reputation conspicuous. Lin Tingzhang, Director in the Ministry of Justice; Feng Fu, Secretary in the Ministry of Works; and Li Yuangu, Secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue, arrived on official missions. Xu Nanjin, Right Provincial Administration Commissioner; Tang Ai, Left Assistant Administration Commissioner; Yu Jin, Right Assistant Administration Commissioner; Ling Yunyi, Li Sui, Li Qiao, Wang Chunze, and Song Shouzhi, Surveillance Vice Commissioners; Gui Dadao, Tang Yaochen, Xu Shi, and Chen Zongyu, Assistant Surveillance Commissioners; and Zheng Weiqing and Wang Hao, Acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioners, all attended to duties outside the examination compound and jointly oversaw the successful completion of the undertaking. Gu Zhongxu, Left Administration Vice Commissioner; Cao Tianyou, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner; and Guan Hai, Acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioner, had already departed to present a congratulatory memorial, but had helped plan the undertaking at its outset and had all contributed to it. In accordance with precedent, their names are also recorded here.

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江武舉鄉試錄

問周官司馬法兵之備書也夷吾一變其
說以速得志於天下而其道僅足以霸
何耶太公韜畧子房所得以說沛公者
也而漢家校理乃以列於儒與道子房
雖得其說亦不多見於用何耶奇正攻
守兵之四事而曰奇正無别攻守一道
豈善師者所已行乎權謀形勢陰陽技
巧兵之四術而或用以勝亦或以敗豈

問：周官、司馬法，兵之備書也。夷吾一變其說，以速得志於天下，而其道僅足以霸，何耶？太公韜畧，子房所得以說沛公者也，而漢家校理乃以列於儒與道。子房雖得其說，亦不多見於用，何耶？奇正攻守，兵之四事，而曰奇正無别，攻守一道，豈善師者所已行乎？權謀形勢陰陽技巧，兵之四術，而或用以勝，亦或以敗，豈
translation_en:
First Session
Mounted archery was tested at a prescribed distance of thirty-five paces. Those who scored four or more hits met the standard.

Second Session
Archery on foot was tested at a prescribed distance of eighty paces. Those who scored two or more hits met the standard.

Third Session
Policy Question
Question: The Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan) and the Methods of the Minister of War (Sima fa) are comprehensive books on military affairs. Yiwu modified their teachings to achieve his ambitions swiftly throughout the realm, yet his methods sufficed only to establish hegemony. Why was this? The Grand Duke’s military strategies were what Zifang acquired and used to advise the Duke of Pei, yet the Han court’s textual editors classified them under the Confucian and Daoist schools. Although Zifang had acquired these teachings, he was seldom seen to put them into practice. Why was this? Unorthodox and orthodox operations, attack and defense, are the four matters of warfare. Yet it is said that unorthodox and orthodox operations are indistinguishable, and that attack and defense follow a single Way. Could this be what skilled commanders have already practiced? Strategic planning, dispositions and strategic advantage, yin and yang, and technical skills are the four military arts. Yet their use sometimes brings victory and sometimes defeat. Could it be that…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江武舉鄉試錄
text:
在兵法有不足信乎古今所稱儒將則
武侯武穆其尤也然作用各有所本而
心術之妙得無有合而爲一者與諸生
誦法有日務要其指歸詳之于篇
論
大明發而萬物皆照
punctuated:
在兵法有不足信乎？古今所稱儒將，則武侯、武穆其尤也。然作用各有所本，而心術之妙，得無有合而爲一者與？諸生誦法有日，務要其指歸，詳之于篇。

論

大明發而萬物皆照。
translation_en:
…does this mean that the methods of warfare contain something unworthy of trust? Among those acclaimed throughout the ages as scholar-generals, Zhuge Liang (Wuhou) and Yue Fei (Wumu) stand foremost. Yet each based his conduct and practice on different foundations: might the subtleties of their inner purposes nevertheless converge as one? You candidates have long studied these methods; be sure to grasp their essential meaning and expound it fully in your essays.

Discourse

The great light shines forth, and all things are illuminated.

text:

善制兵者期於不可敗而已而功不與焉

惟期於不可敗也故其爲制不得不曲而
===

始也惟期於不可致也故其爲用不得不
隱而變變也者所以疑其心志使欲備之
而無從也是故師有常勝之理無常勝之
形有不敗之將無不敗之法惟本之以仁
義濟之以權變動之以忠誠而運之以智
勇則常勝之道在我其一不效猶足以榮

punctuated:
第叅場
策

善制兵者，期於不可敗而已，而功不與焉；善用兵者，期於不可致而已，而法不與焉。惟期於不可敗也，故其爲制不得不曲而繁。繁也者，所以分其視聽，使欲乘之而無始也。惟期於不可致也，故其爲用不得不隱而變。變也者，所以疑其心志，使欲備之而無從也。是故師有常勝之理，無常勝之形；有不敗之將，無不敗之法。惟本之以仁義，濟之以權變，動之以忠誠，而運之以智勇，則常勝之道在我。其一不效，猶足以榮於天下。豈若急功尚詐，雖有大利而爲後

Third Session
Policy Essay
Zhang Xun
He scored eight hits in mounted archery and four hits in archery on foot.

Those skilled at organizing troops aim only to make them incapable of defeat; achievements do not enter into it. Those skilled at employing troops aim only to ensure that they cannot be drawn into the enemy’s designs; fixed methods do not enter into it. Precisely because they aim to be incapable of defeat, their arrangements must be intricate and elaborate. Such elaboration divides the enemy’s attention, leaving him no opening from which to exploit them. Precisely because they aim not to be drawn into the enemy’s designs, their operations must be concealed and changeable. Such changes unsettle the enemy’s mind and resolve, leaving him no way to prepare against them. Thus, armies have principles of constant victory, but no configuration that constantly brings victory; there are undefeated commanders, but no unfailing methods. Only by taking benevolence and righteousness as the foundation, supplementing them with expedient adaptation, acting from loyalty and sincerity, and directing operations with wisdom and courage can we hold the way to constant victory in our own hands. Even if one of these fails to prove effective, this is still sufficient to bring honor throughout the realm. title: 嘉靖四十年浙江武舉鄉試錄
text:
世所羞稱者哉嘗慨夫世之談兵者貴速
效而忘大道也執事發策首及周官司馬
法可謂有王佐之心而達於當世之務矣
顧介胄之士何足仰副惟嘗讀其書而竊
窺其意蓋所以脩內治外而不欲求逞於
天下者也彼先王所以齊民之具不越乎
仁義禮樂而已以爲不足以消其悖戾好
爭之心而誅討作焉小者致之市朝大者
===
陳諸原野無非以奉天道而威不軌故堯
舜之世至治之極然非四罪則人不服其
義殷周以兵定天下矣當其干戈載戢教
以文德而猶立司馬之官設六軍之衆因
井田以制軍賦命連師正牧以簡車徒定
春蒐夏苗秋獮冬狩以講武事通畿之師
大司馬遞而征之以更勞逸其法曰五人
爲伍五伍爲兩萬二千五百人而爲軍二
punctuated: 世所羞稱者哉？嘗慨夫世之談兵者，貴速效而忘大道也。執事發策，首及周官司馬法，可謂有王佐之心，而達於當世之務矣。顧介胄之士，何足仰副？惟嘗讀其書而竊窺其意，蓋所以脩內治外，而不欲求逞於天下者也。彼先王所以齊民之具，不越乎仁義禮樂而已。以爲不足以消其悖戾好爭之心，而誅討作焉。小者致之市朝，大者陳諸原野，無非以奉天道而威不軌。故堯舜之世，至治之極，然非四罪，則人不服其義。殷周以兵定天下矣，當其干戈載戢，教以文德，而猶立司馬之官，設六軍之衆，因井田以制軍賦，命連師正牧以簡車徒，定春蒐、夏苗、秋獮、冬狩以講武事。通畿之師，大司馬遞而征之，以更勞逸。其法曰：五人爲伍，五伍爲兩，萬二千五百人而爲軍。二
translation_en:
…whom later generations would be ashamed to mention? I have often lamented that those who discuss warfare prize swift results and forget the Great Way. In issuing your policy question, you began with the Offices of Zhou and the Methods of the Minister of War (Sima fa). You may indeed be said to possess the aspiration to assist a true king and to understand the affairs of the present age. Yet how could a man in helmet and armor such as myself adequately meet your expectations? I have merely read these books and ventured to glimpse their meaning: their purpose is to cultivate internal governance and bring order to external affairs, without seeking to impose one's will upon the world.

The means by which the former kings brought their people into harmony extended no further than benevolence, righteousness, ritual, and music. Because they considered these insufficient to dispel the people's perversity and fondness for contention, punitive action arose. Lesser offenders were brought to the marketplace or court for punishment; against greater offenders, forces were arrayed in the open fields. All this served to uphold the Way of Heaven and overawe the unruly. Thus the age of Yao and Shun marked the pinnacle of good government; nevertheless, without the punishment of the four malefactors, the people would not have submitted to their justice.

The Yin and Zhou dynasties pacified the realm by force of arms. Once they had put away their weapons and instructed the people through civil virtue, they nevertheless established the office of Minister of War and maintained the forces of the Six Armies. They based military levies on the well-field system and charged the territorial heads—the lian, shi, zheng, and mu—with selecting chariots and infantry. They prescribed the spring sou, summer miao, autumn xian, and winter shou hunts to practice military affairs. The Grand Minister of War called up the forces throughout the royal domain in rotation, so that toil and rest alternated. Their regulations stated: five men formed a squad; five squads formed a platoon; twelve thousand five hundred men formed an army. Two…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江武舉鄉試錄
text:
百五十十取三焉而爲奇其餘七以爲正
四奇四正而八陣生焉蓋多爲之曲折以
盡其數以極其變鈎連蟠屈使敵無所窺
利則強本遏萌以靜制變之大畧也周室
既東諸侯強大而國自爲政齊侯伋以其
法傳於桓公之世管仲相之以爲脩甲繕
兵示人以備則不足以速得志於天下於
是一變其法以就簡直雖於軌里連鄉之
===
稱戎伍卒旅之數視周制不遠然三分其
國以爲三軍軍萬人焉公將其一高子將
其二皆齊之以一切之令緩急足以相死
非若周之人容保而優游之也其效雖足
以一匡天下存三亡國然先王所以不得
已而制兵之意既以蕩然後世所稱善戰
之士以愚爲利者將日求勝則仲非首亂
者哉無惑乎穰苴再變而權詐尚因勢輔
punctuated:
百五十，十取三焉而爲奇，其餘七以爲正。四奇四正而八陣生焉。蓋多爲之曲折，以盡其數，以極其變，鈎連蟠屈，使敵無所窺利，則強本遏萌、以靜制變之大畧也。

周室既東，諸侯強大，而國自爲政。齊侯伋以其法傳於桓公之世，管仲相之，以爲脩甲繕兵，示人以備，則不足以速得志於天下，於是一變其法，以就簡直。雖於軌里連鄉之稱、戎伍卒旅之數，視周制不遠，然三分其國以爲三軍，軍萬人焉。公將其一，高子將其二，皆齊之以一切之令，緩急足以相死，非若周之人容保而優游之也。其效雖足以一匡天下，存三亡國，然先王所以不得已而制兵之意，既以蕩然。後世所稱善戰之士，以愚爲利者，將日求勝，則仲非首亂者哉？無惑乎穰苴再變而權詐尚，因勢輔
translation_en:
…hundred and fifty. Of every ten, three were assigned to the extraordinary forces, and the remaining seven to the regular forces. Four extraordinary and four regular formations produced the Eight Formations. Their arrangements were made intricate and winding to exhaust all numerical possibilities and encompass every variation; linked and coiled together, they left the enemy no opening to exploit. This was the broad strategy of strengthening the foundations, checking trouble at its inception, and controlling change through stillness.

After the Zhou royal house moved east, the regional lords grew powerful, and each state governed itself. Ji, Marquis of Qi, transmitted these methods down to the age of Duke Huan. Guan Zhong, serving as his minister, considered that repairing armor and putting weapons in order, thereby displaying preparedness, would not suffice to achieve their ambitions swiftly throughout the realm. He therefore altered the system to make it simpler and more direct. Although the names of its territorial units—gui, li, lian, and xiang—and the numerical organization of its military units—rong, wu, zu, and lü [?]—differed little from Zhou institutions, he divided the state into three parts to create three armies, each of ten thousand men. The duke commanded one, and Gaozi commanded the other two [?]. All were brought into uniform order by categorical commands, so that in an emergency they were ready to die for one another. This differed from the Zhou practice of accommodating and protecting the people and allowing them ease and freedom. Though its results sufficed to set the realm in order and preserve three states facing extinction, the former kings’ intention in establishing armed forces only out of necessity had already been utterly swept away. Those whom later generations called skilled warriors, who profited by deceiving others, would seek victory day after day. Was Guan Zhong, then, not the first to sow disorder? No wonder Rangju altered the system again and stratagems and deception came to be esteemed, while those who exploited circumstances and accommodated …

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江武舉鄉試錄
text:
時之士以其術轉相傾覆皆足以禽敵立
勝垂著載籍然非有安制矜節之理斯爲
下矣漢興以寛仁之厚準古立法命張韓
序次兵考定著三十五家而言不及三畧
則太公之法微矣班固序書自風后力牧
下迨種蠡悉載兵家而獨以周史六弢列
之於儒以太公謀言列之於道則韜畧雖
傳而非當世之所用可知矣所謂然者漢
===
襲秦後率以都隷之法教其將帥無非譎
詐以求速勝宜其所尚在彼而不在此史
氏謂張良與沛公遇於留以太公兵法說
之非說以法也說以法之意也執事謂良
得其說而不多見於用非良未嘗用之也
用之而善藏焉者也說者謂其授於圯上
而後世復得於枕中皆怪誕無據惟觀其
借箸之畫首發八難跡武王造周之業以
punctuated: 時之士，以其術轉相傾覆，皆足以禽敵立勝，垂著載籍。然非有安制矜節之理，斯爲下矣。漢興，以寛仁之厚，準古立法，命張韓序次兵，考定著三十五家，而言不及三畧，則太公之法微矣。班固序書，自風后力牧下迨種蠡，悉載兵家，而獨以周史六弢列之於儒，以太公謀言列之於道，則韜畧雖傳，而非當世之所用可知矣。所謂然者，漢襲秦後，率以都隷之法教其將帥，無非譎詐以求速勝，宜其所尚在彼而不在此。史氏謂張良與沛公遇於留，以太公兵法說之，非說以法也，說以法之意也。執事謂良得其說，而不多見於用，非良未嘗用之也，用之而善藏焉者也。說者謂其授於圯上，而後世復得於枕中，皆怪誕無據。惟觀其借箸之畫，首發八難，跡武王造周之業，以
translation_en:
…men who adapted to their times used these techniques to overthrow one another in turn. All were capable of capturing enemies and securing immediate victories, leaving their achievements recorded for posterity. Yet they lacked principles of stable institutions and disciplined restraint [?], and thus were inferior.

When the Han arose, with its generous spirit of leniency and benevolence, it established methods modeled on antiquity. It ordered Zhang Liang and Han Xin to arrange military writings and, after examination, establish a collection of thirty-five schools. Yet no mention was made of the Three Strategies (Sanlüe): the methods of the Grand Duke (Taigong) had thus fallen into obscurity. In his bibliographical account, Ban Gu included everyone from Feng Hou and Li Mu down to Wen Zhong and Fan Li among the military writers. Yet he placed the Six Bow Cases of the Zhou Historian (Zhou shi liutao) among the Confucian writings, and the Grand Duke’s Plans and Sayings among the Daoist writings. We can therefore see that, although these strategic teachings were transmitted, they were not employed in that age. The reason was that the Han succeeded the Qin and generally instructed its commanders in the methods of metropolitan convict laborers [?]. These amounted to nothing but deception in pursuit of swift victory. Naturally, what they esteemed lay in those methods rather than these.

The historian says that Zhang Liang met the Duke of Pei at Liu and persuaded him through the Grand Duke’s Art of War. He did not persuade him through its rules themselves, but through their underlying intent. You, sir, say that Liang grasped its teachings, yet seldom visibly put them into practice. It was not that Liang never used them: he used them but was adept at concealing their application. Accounts claiming that the teachings were imparted to him on a bridge, and that later generations recovered them from inside a pillow, are all fantastic and without foundation. Consider only his plan explained with borrowed chopsticks: he began by setting out eight objections, tracing King Wu’s achievement in founding the Zhou in order to …

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江武舉鄉試錄
text:
規高帝所不足至於沙中定議則其尊賢
而尚功者也商山招致則其養老以致民
者也尼良之善用於沛公孰非兵法所有
其後諸葛獨識其遺制以爲可用以取天
下故以十二萬之衆迭任其八相持數歲
卒不能得志於魏豈以八陣爲非逐利制
勝之具耶武穆用兵神武所向無敵史稱
其素好左氏誦法孫吾則其作用固異於
===
諸葛然當康王始立首建恢復以繫中原
之望從事統領再倡定謀以强河北之師
則豈權謀之說所能盡哉論者謂武侯兵
法本於六韜而其節制則得於左氏故武
侯之師極天下之至深武侯兵法本於左
氏而運用則得諸六韜故武穆之師極天
下之至變是皆不足以知王佐之心者也
二公之心皆以興復爲己任誓無兩立觀
punctuated: 規高帝所不足。至於沙中定議，則其尊賢而尚功者也；商山招致，則其養老以致民者也。尼良之善用於沛公，孰非兵法所有？其後諸葛獨識其遺制，以爲可用以取天下，故以十二萬之衆迭任其八，相持數歲，卒不能得志於魏，豈以八陣爲非逐利制勝之具耶？武穆用兵神武，所向無敵。史稱其素好左氏，誦法孫吾，則其作用固異於諸葛。然當康王始立，首建恢復以繫中原之望；從事統領，再倡定謀以强河北之師，則豈權謀之說所能盡哉？論者謂武侯兵法本於六韜，而其節制則得於左氏，故武侯之師極天下之至深；武侯兵法本於左氏，而運用則得諸六韜，故武穆之師極天下之至變。是皆不足以知王佐之心者也。二公之心皆以興復爲己任，誓無兩立。觀
translation_en:
…to point out where Emperor Gao fell short. As for settling the deliberations on the sandbank, this exemplified honoring the worthy and esteeming merit; inviting the elders from Mount Shang exemplified caring for the aged so as to attract the people. Zhang Liang’s skillful application of these principles in serving the Duke of Pei [?]: which of these actions was not encompassed by the methods of warfare?

Later, Zhuge Liang alone understood the surviving system and believed it could be used to win the empire. Thus, with a force of 120,000, he employed its eight divisions in rotation [?]. He maintained the confrontation for several years but ultimately could not achieve his aims against Wei. Does this mean that the Eight Formations were not an instrument for pursuing advantage and securing victory?

Wumu [Yue Fei] commanded armies with divine martial prowess and was invincible wherever he advanced. The histories state that he had always delighted in the Zuo Commentary and recited and emulated Sunzi and Wuzi [the transcription reads Sun-Wu as 孫吾]. His practical methods therefore certainly differed from Zhuge Liang’s. Yet when the Prince of Kang first ascended the throne, he was the first to propose restoration, sustaining the hopes of the Central Plain; while serving in military command, he again urged the adoption of a settled strategy to strengthen the forces in Hebei. How could theories of expedient stratagems fully account for this?

Commentators say that the military methods of Wuhou [Zhuge Liang] were rooted in the Six Secret Teachings, while his discipline and organization derived from the Zuo Commentary; hence Wuhou’s army attained the utmost profundity under Heaven. They further say that Wuhou’s military methods [the text repeats Wuhou here, apparently meaning Wumu] were rooted in the Zuo Commentary, while their practical application derived from the Six Secret Teachings; hence Wumu’s army attained the utmost adaptability under Heaven. None of these judgments suffices to understand the intentions of men capable of assisting a true king. Both men took restoration as their own responsibility and swore never to coexist with the enemy. title: 嘉靖四十年浙江武舉鄉試錄
text:
其糾合忠義之舉即集思廣忠之謨也經
畧西京之密奏即出師二表之遺意也惟
勢之所值武侯僅足以不敗故緩而持之
以俟其成而得於司馬法之意多武穆計
足以決勝故急而圖之以奪其心而得於
孫吳之意多至於成功則天也雖二公不
得而與焉由此觀之談兵者以知德爲上
知變次之知利爲下若所論於奇正攻守
===
之理則固知德者所不廢而權謀形勢陰
陽技巧之術雖善變者亦難取必於一槩
也唐太宗曰敵意其奇則吾正擊之敵意
其正則吾奇擊之使敵勢常虛我勢常實
則虛實無形自我示之耳兵法所謂形人
者也又曰守之法要在示敵以不足攻之
法要在示敵以有餘示以不足則敵必乘
而攻示以有餘則敵必怯而守是攻守無
punctuated: 其糾合忠義之舉，即集思廣忠之謨也；經畧西京之密奏，即出師二表之遺意也。惟勢之所值，武侯僅足以不敗，故緩而持之，以俟其成，而得於司馬法之意多；武穆計足以決勝，故急而圖之，以奪其心，而得於孫吳之意多。至於成功，則天也，雖二公不得而與焉。由此觀之，談兵者以知德爲上，知變次之，知利爲下。若所論於奇正攻守之理，則固知德者所不廢；而權謀、形勢、陰陽、技巧之術，雖善變者亦難取必於一槩也。唐太宗曰：「敵意其奇，則吾正擊之；敵意其正，則吾奇擊之。使敵勢常虛，我勢常實，則虛實無形，自我示之耳。」兵法所謂形人者也。又曰：「守之法，要在示敵以不足；攻之法，要在示敵以有餘。示以不足，則敵必乘而攻；示以有餘，則敵必怯而守。」是攻守無
translation_en:
…his efforts to rally the loyal and righteous were precisely a plan to pool deliberations and broaden loyalty [?]; his confidential memorial on securing the western capital embodied the intention bequeathed in the two Memorials on Dispatching the Army. Given the circumstances he faced, the Marquis of Wu (Zhuge Liang) could do no more than avoid defeat. He therefore proceeded slowly and held firm, awaiting success, drawing more heavily on the principles of the Methods of the Minister of War (Sima fa). Wumu (Yue Fei), however, had plans sufficient to secure victory. He therefore pressed urgently ahead to break the enemy’s resolve, drawing more heavily on the principles of Sun Wu and Wu Qi. As for ultimate success, that lay with Heaven: even these two men could not determine it. Viewed in this light, among those who discuss warfare, understanding virtue ranks highest, understanding adaptation comes next, and understanding advantage ranks lowest. The principles of unorthodox and orthodox operations, attack and defense discussed here are certainly not neglected by those who understand virtue. Yet even those adept at adaptation cannot expect assured results from applying a single standard to the arts of strategic calculation, dispositions and circumstances, yin and yang, and technical skills.
Emperor Taizong of the Tang said: “When the enemy expects an unorthodox operation, I strike with an orthodox one; when the enemy expects an orthodox operation, I strike with an unorthodox one. Keep the enemy’s position always empty and our own always substantial. Emptiness and substance thus have no fixed form; they depend solely on what we display.” This is what the military writings call making the enemy reveal his dispositions. He also said: “The essential method of defense is to show the enemy insufficiency; the essential method of attack is to show the enemy abundance. Show insufficiency, and the enemy will certainly seize the opportunity to attack; show abundance, and the enemy will certainly grow fearful and defend.” Thus attack and defense have no…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江武舉鄉試錄
text:
定自我致之耳兵法所謂致人者也觀之
晉與楚戰欒枝輿柴以遁楚師馳之蓋以
正爲奇也韓信還軍水上佯棄旗鼓而趙
以就襲蓋以奇爲正也亞夫堅壁以備吳
楚之師直俟引退而出精兵追擊其後盡
虜其軍則守非所以爲攻乎武穆說張所
以河北之議直俟犯鎮而後迭出以撓其
師而金人終不能窺河南則攻非所以爲
守乎故曰攻是守之機守是攻之策大衆
所合爲正將所自出爲奇信乎不可以歧
而言矣兵之先計而後戰者謂之權謀孫
臏馬陵之役王恢馬邑之詐是也然臏以
斃敵而恢以自殺其身權謀其足恃乎兵
之後發而先至者謂之形勢趙奢閼與之
救孟德烏巢之役是也然奢以敗秦而曹
以自蹶其師形勢不足恃矣兵有明五勝
punctuated: 定，自我致之耳，兵法所謂致人者也。觀之晉與楚戰，欒枝輿柴以遁，楚師馳之，蓋以正爲奇也。韓信還軍水上，佯棄旗鼓，而趙以就襲，蓋以奇爲正也。亞夫堅壁以備吳楚之師，直俟引退，而出精兵追擊其後，盡虜其軍，則守非所以爲攻乎？武穆說張所以河北之議，直俟犯鎮，而後迭出以撓其師，而金人終不能窺河南，則攻非所以爲守乎？故曰：「攻是守之機，守是攻之策。」大衆所合爲正，將所自出爲奇，信乎不可以歧而言矣。兵之先計而後戰者謂之權謀，孫臏馬陵之役、王恢馬邑之詐是也。然臏以斃敵，而恢以自殺其身，權謀其足恃乎？兵之後發而先至者謂之形勢，趙奢閼與之救、孟德烏巢之役是也。然奢以敗秦，而曹以自蹶其師，形勢不足恃矣。兵有明五勝
translation_en:
…have no fixed form; I myself bring them about. This is what the military classics call making others act at one’s bidding. Consider the battle between Jin and Chu: Luan Zhi dragged brushwood behind his chariots as he fled, and the Chu army pursued him. This was using the orthodox as the unorthodox. Han Xin returned his army to the waterside and pretended to abandon his banners and drums, whereupon the Zhao troops advanced to attack. This was using the unorthodox as the orthodox. Zhou Yafu fortified his camp against the armies of Wu and Chu, waiting until they withdrew before sending picked troops to pursue them from the rear and capture their entire army. Was this not using defense to carry out an attack? Yue Fei, posthumously titled Wumu, urged Zhang Suo to adopt his proposal concerning Hebei: wait until the enemy attacked the garrisons, then repeatedly sally out to harass their army. In the end, the Jin forces could not even threaten Henan. Was this not using attack to carry out defense? Thus it is said: “Attack is the pivot of defense; defense is the strategy of attack.” What the mass of troops undertakes together is orthodox; what the commander independently devises is unorthodox. Indeed, these cannot be discussed as separate things.

In warfare, planning first and fighting afterward is called strategic calculation. Sun Bin’s campaign at Maling and Wang Hui’s deception at Mayi are examples. Yet Sun Bin thereby destroyed his enemy, whereas Wang Hui thereby brought about his own suicide. Can strategic calculation really be relied upon? In warfare, setting out later but arriving first is called strategic disposition. Zhao She’s relief of Eyu and Cao Cao, styled Mengde’s, campaign at Wuchao are examples. Yet Zhao She thereby defeated Qin, whereas Cao thereby brought his own army to ruin [?]. Strategic disposition cannot be relied upon. In warfare, there are those who understand the five phases’ successive conquests…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江武舉鄉試錄
text:
而假於鬼神者謂之陰陽然西伯以卜而
獲霸王之輔漢武以卜而失貳師之將則
陰陽者不過神其說以使愚者也兵有積
機關以立攻守之勝者謂之技巧然巫臣
教吳以車戰通於上國房琯亦用其法以
敗於陳濤則技巧者不過便習其器械以
擊不備者也如是而謂四者非兵之術固
不可然謂之必勝之術則惑矣何者兵之
變固不可以勝窮而敵之所遇又不可以
逆定故孫武之書蘇氏常稱其詞約而意
盡然自爲之而自不能用以取敗北况祖
其餘論者耶方今之務惟兵爲急若繩以
周官之法求臻仁義之理則宋襄之仁而
不可爲也若徂之以慶賞道之以刑罰使
民好戰以要利於上則秦法之烈而不可
爲也無已其求之制節乎然齊以十五鄉
punctuated:
而假於鬼神者，謂之陰陽。然西伯以卜而獲霸王之輔，漢武以卜而失貳師之將，則陰陽者，不過神其說以使愚者也。兵有積機關以立攻守之勝者，謂之技巧。然巫臣教吳以車戰，通於上國；房琯亦用其法，以敗於陳濤。則技巧者，不過便習其器械以擊不備者也。如是而謂四者非兵之術，固不可；然謂之必勝之術，則惑矣。何者？兵之變，固不可以勝窮，而敵之所遇，又不可以逆定。故孫武之書，蘇氏常稱其詞約而意盡，然自爲之而自不能用，以取敗北，况祖其餘論者耶？

方今之務，惟兵爲急。若繩以周官之法，求臻仁義之理，則宋襄之仁而不可爲也。若徂之以慶賞，道之以刑罰，使民好戰以要利於上，則秦法之烈而不可爲也。無已，其求之制節乎？然齊以十五鄉
translation_en:
…and draws upon ghosts and spirits: this is called the yin-yang approach to warfare. Yet through divination the Lord of the West obtained an assistant who helped him achieve hegemony and kingship, while Emperor Wu of Han, through divination, lost his General of Ershi. Thus the yin-yang approach merely invests its doctrines with supernatural authority to command the ignorant. Warfare that accumulates mechanical devices to secure victory in attack and defense is called technical skill. Yet when Wuchen taught Wu chariot warfare, Wu gained access to the central states; Fang Guan likewise used this method, only to suffer defeat at Chentao. Thus technical skill merely consists in becoming proficient with weapons and equipment in order to strike the unprepared. Given this, one certainly cannot say that these four approaches are not arts of warfare; but to call them arts that ensure victory is a delusion. Why? The transformations of warfare cannot be exhausted, and the circumstances in which one encounters the enemy cannot be determined beforehand. Thus Master Su often praised Sun Wu’s book for its concise wording and comprehensive meaning. Yet its author himself could not put it into practice and suffered defeat—how much less could those who take his surviving discussions as their guide?

Among the pressing concerns of the present day, military affairs alone are most urgent. If we apply the standards of the Offices of Zhou and seek to attain the principles of benevolence and righteousness, this would amount to the benevolence of Duke Xiang of Song and cannot be practiced. If we spur people on [?] with rewards and guide them with punishments, making them delight in warfare so as to seek benefits from their superiors, this would amount to the severity of Qin’s laws and likewise cannot be practiced. If there is no alternative, should we seek the answer in regulation and restraint? Yet Qi, with its fifteen townships…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江武舉鄉試錄
text:
之民皆有授田而後責其調發五屬之地
皆以農居之而不責其供輸是以民無耗
費之患兵無不給之憂能有餘力以致其
死令也富民之田既不可奪則箕斂之政
自不容已兵之於民日見其相病而或强
以相資制兵者之所以難也所恃
國家全盛統一區宇屏翰之臣爲憲於上干
城之士戮力於下雖南夷犯順式勞薄伐
===
固未有釆芑之咏輿於畓畝豈愚以輿廝
之役而敢遽議乎大計哉惟執事進敎之
又
張一鶴
馬上中六箭
步下中三箭
兵非得已而用之也故其法語之爲至詳
而用之爲至隱何也戡亂定難者兵也操
punctuated:
之民皆有授田，而後責其調發；五屬之地，皆以農居之，而不責其供輸。是以民無耗費之患，兵無不給之憂，能有餘力以致其死令也。富民之田既不可奪，則箕斂之政自不容已。兵之於民，日見其相病，而或强以相資，制兵者之所以難也。所恃國家全盛，統一區宇，屏翰之臣爲憲於上，干城之士戮力於下。雖南夷犯順，式勞薄伐，固未有《釆芑》之咏輿於畓畝。豈愚以輿廝之役，而敢遽議乎大計哉？惟執事進敎之。
又。
張一鶴。
馬上中六箭，步下中三箭。
兵非得已而用之也，故其法語之爲至詳，而用之爲至隱，何也？戡亂定難者，兵也；操
translation_en:
…the people were all allotted land before being required to answer military levies. In the territories of the five dependencies, all were settled as farmers and were not required to furnish supplies. Thus the people suffered no depletion of their resources, and the troops had no worries about inadequate provision; they had strength to spare to obey orders unto death. Since the lands of wealthy households cannot be seized, policies of sweeping exaction cannot cease. The army and the people are daily seen to impair one another, yet they are sometimes forced to sustain one another: this is what makes organizing an army difficult.
Our reliance is upon the state’s flourishing strength and its unification of the realm. Ministers who serve as its bulwarks set standards above, while warriors who serve as its shields and walls exert themselves together below. Although the southern barbarians have defied imperial authority, occasioning the toil of punitive expeditions, no song of “Gathering Millet” (Cai qi) has yet arisen among the fields [?]. How could an ignorant man such as I, serving in a menial transport role, dare abruptly to discuss grand strategy? I ask only that you, honored examiners, grant me further instruction.
Another answer.
Zhang Yihe hit the target with six arrows on horseback and three arrows on foot.
Armed force is employed only when there is no alternative. Thus its methods are explained in the greatest detail, yet their application is profoundly subtle. Why is this? What quells disorder and settles crises is armed force; the wielding…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江武舉鄉試錄
text:
縱闔闢者法也神而明之不離於法而不
泥乎法者心也故天下無常勝之兵而有
不可敗之將無必勝之法而有不可窮之
機彼强弱老少輕重長短各以其敵而卒
致於吾前均不可以預圖者故隨機應變
因變制敵循於法之內者勝也神於法之
外者亦勝也動乎九天之上藏於九地之
下古稱良將能收安攘之績而威敵於莫
===
敢嚮邇者何哉機妙於心而所以爲作用
之本者誠非尋常智識之可得而窺也今
夫兵者天之義氣也於五行爲金於時爲
秋然五行之運屈伸往來無始呼吸寒燠
無端不終朝而煦然肅然莫能爲象者天
固不能定執其機夫固歲功之所由成也
五材之運於民無以異於五行之運於天
也而顧欲執其法則亦何以示之武而爲
punctuated:
縱闔闢者，法也；神而明之，不離於法而不泥乎法者，心也。故天下無常勝之兵，而有不可敗之將；無必勝之法，而有不可窮之機。彼强弱老少、輕重長短，各以其敵而卒致於吾前，均不可以預圖者。故隨機應變，因變制敵，循於法之內者勝也，神於法之外者亦勝也。動乎九天之上，藏於九地之下，古稱良將，能收安攘之績，而威敵於莫敢嚮邇者，何哉？機妙於心，而所以爲作用之本者，誠非尋常智識之可得而窺也。
今夫兵者，天之義氣也，於五行爲金，於時爲秋。然五行之運，屈伸往來無始，呼吸寒燠無端，不終朝而煦然肅然，莫能爲象者，天固不能定執其機，夫固歲功之所由成也。五材之運於民，無以異於五行之運於天也。而顧欲執其法，則亦何以示之武，而爲
translation_en:
…maneuvering, closing, and opening are matters of method; what makes these operations wondrous and comprehensible, neither departing from method nor becoming bound by it, is the mind. Thus, under Heaven there are no armies that invariably win, but there are generals who cannot be defeated; there are no methods that guarantee victory, but there are opportunities for action that cannot be exhausted. The enemy’s strengths and weaknesses, old and young, light and heavy forces, and long and short weapons—all vary with the opponent and suddenly confront us; none can be planned for in advance. Therefore, one responds to changing circumstances as opportunities arise and exploits those changes to subdue the enemy. Those who follow established methods achieve victory; those who exercise inspired skill beyond those methods likewise achieve victory. Moving above the ninth heaven and concealing themselves beneath the ninth depth of the earth, the renowned generals of antiquity secured peace at home and repelled external threats, overawing their enemies so that none dared approach. Why was this? Their subtle grasp of opportunity lay in the mind, and what formed the foundation of their actions was truly beyond the scrutiny of ordinary intelligence and understanding.
Now warfare is Heaven’s vital force of righteousness: among the Five Phases it corresponds to metal, and among the seasons to autumn. Yet in the movement of the Five Phases, contraction and expansion, coming and going have no beginning; exhalation and inhalation, cold and warmth have no fixed starting point. Before a morning has passed, there may be gentle warmth or stern chill, beyond anyone’s power to represent. Heaven itself cannot hold this dynamic to a fixed course; indeed, it is through this that the work of the year is accomplished. The employment of the five materials among the people is no different from the movement of the Five Phases in Heaven. Yet if one insists on adhering rigidly to methods, how can one thereby display martial might and serve as…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江武舉鄉試錄
text:
威天下者之所恃哉譬則醫然兵之有法
猶醫之有方也表裏虚實君臣佐使則因
其病而藥之非惟方之不能盡抑醫之莫
能知也善兵者師中之盧扁而以藥天下
之膏肓者也顧徒執一方而醫之其何以
爲三軍之司命乎周官司馬法兵之備書
也兵寓於農有事則爲伍兩卒旅之役無
事則爲比閭族黨之居誠致太平之迹也
===
豈徒爲兵計哉管夷吾欲速得志於天下
一變而爲内政軍令之寄而其道僅足以
取威定伯者麟趾關雎之意微也太公韜
畧兵之善謀也其鷹揚之績以仁義爲尚
以吊伐爲先雖有八卦五行陰陽三畧之
象豈徒以詭取勝哉張子房粗得其順天
應人之意而爲報仇爲韓之舉亦足稱爲
儒者之氣象者黄老雜伯之機勝也奇正
punctuated: 威天下者之所恃哉？譬則醫然，兵之有法，猶醫之有方也。表裏虚實，君臣佐使，則因其病而藥之，非惟方之不能盡，抑醫之莫能知也。善兵者，師中之盧扁，而以藥天下之膏肓者也。顧徒執一方而醫之，其何以爲三軍之司命乎？《周官》《司馬法》，兵之備書也。兵寓於農，有事則爲伍兩卒旅之役，無事則爲比閭族黨之居，誠致太平之迹也。豈徒爲兵計哉？管夷吾欲速得志於天下，一變而爲内政軍令之寄，而其道僅足以取威定伯者，《麟趾》《關雎》之意微也。《太公韜畧》，兵之善謀也。其鷹揚之績，以仁義爲尚，以吊伐爲先，雖有八卦五行陰陽三畧之象，豈徒以詭取勝哉？張子房粗得其順天應人之意，而爲報仇爲韓之舉，亦足稱爲儒者之氣象者，黄老雜伯之機勝也。奇正
translation_en:
…that those who overawe the realm rely upon? Consider the analogy of medicine: military methods are like medical prescriptions. Whether a disorder is external or internal, deficient or excessive, and how drugs serve as sovereign, minister, assistant, or envoy—all require administering medicine according to the illness. Not only can prescriptions not encompass every case; even physicians cannot know them all. One skilled in warfare is a Lu or a Bian among the troops, a physician treating the realm’s most deep-seated maladies. If he merely clings to a single prescription in treating them, how can he be entrusted with the lives of the entire army?

The Offices of Zhou and The Methods of the Minister of War are comprehensive books on military affairs. Soldiers were incorporated within the farming population. When military affairs arose, they served in units of five, twenty-five, one hundred, and five hundred; otherwise, they lived in neighborhood groupings of five, twenty-five, one hundred, and five hundred households. These were indeed arrangements that brought about Great Peace. How could they have been intended merely for military purposes? Guan Yiwu wished swiftly to realize his ambitions throughout the realm. He transformed this system, lodging military commands within civil administration. Yet his methods sufficed only to acquire authority and establish hegemony, because the spirit of “The Qilin’s Hooves” and “The Ospreys Cry” was weak in them.

The Grand Duke’s Military Strategies contains excellent military counsel. His achievements, soaring like a hawk, exalted benevolence and righteousness and gave priority to comforting the afflicted and punishing the guilty. Though it includes configurations of the Eight Trigrams, Five Phases, yin and yang, and the Three Strategies, how could its sole purpose have been victory through deception? Zhang Zifang roughly grasped its intention of following Heaven and responding to the people. His actions to avenge wrongs and serve the state of Han could also be said to display the bearing of a Confucian scholar; yet the workings of Huang-Lao thought mingled with hegemonic methods predominated in him [?]. Unorthodox and orthodox operations…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江武舉鄉試錄
text:
攻守兵之有四事也而法則未始或分也
或卽正以爲奇或卽奇以爲正或善攻而
敵不知所守或善守而敵不知所攻厚幣
甲詞以見推不爲屈也疾走大梁以解圍
不爲襲也雪夜冐險以趨利不爲亟也輕
裘緩帶以視師不爲慢也所謂奇正無別
攻守一道豈非已行之驗與權變形勢陰
陽技巧兵之有四術也而法則未始或執
===
也故同一權謀也孫臏之料龐涓何其神
而王恢用於馬邑則敗同一形勢也趙奢
之據北山何其捷而曹瞞次於烏林則危
陰陽所當尚也然或以甲子而敗或以往
亡而興技巧所必用也然或師車戰而通
上國或用車戰而覆王師所謂或用以敗
或用以勝豈非用法之過歟於漢得一武
侯焉西出祁山而不顧南擒孟獲而不誅
punctuated: 攻守，兵之有四事也，而法則未始或分也。或卽正以爲奇，或卽奇以爲正；或善攻而敵不知所守，或善守而敵不知所攻。厚幣甲詞以見推，不爲屈也；疾走大梁以解圍，不爲襲也；雪夜冐險以趨利，不爲亟也；輕裘緩帶以視師，不爲慢也。所謂奇正無別，攻守一道，豈非已行之驗與？權變、形勢、陰陽、技巧，兵之有四術也，而法則未始或執也。故同一權謀也，孫臏之料龐涓何其神，而王恢用於馬邑則敗；同一形勢也，趙奢之據北山何其捷，而曹瞞次於烏林則危。陰陽所當尚也，然或以甲子而敗，或以往亡而興；技巧所必用也，然或師車戰而通上國，或用車戰而覆王師。所謂或用以敗，或用以勝，豈非用法之過歟？於漢得一武侯焉，西出祁山而不顧，南擒孟獲而不誅。
translation_en:
…attack and defense: these make up the four affairs of warfare, yet their governing principles have never been separate. Sometimes the orthodox becomes the unorthodox, and sometimes the unorthodox becomes the orthodox. Sometimes one attacks so skillfully that the enemy does not know where to defend; sometimes one defends so skillfully that the enemy does not know where to attack. Offering lavish gifts and words [?] to secure another’s support does not constitute submission; rushing to Daliang to relieve a siege does not constitute a surprise assault; braving danger on a snowy night to gain an advantage does not constitute undue haste; inspecting the troops in a light fur robe with a loosely fastened belt does not constitute negligence. As the saying goes, the unorthodox and orthodox are not distinct, and attack and defense follow a single Way. Are these not proofs drawn from actual practice?

Adaptation to circumstances, strategic configuration, yin and yang, and technical skill constitute the four arts of warfare, yet their governing principles have never been rigidly fixed. Thus, although the same art of strategic planning was involved, how marvelous was Sun Bin’s assessment of Pang Juan, whereas Wang Hui’s employment of it at Mayi ended in defeat! Although the same art of strategic configuration was involved, how swift was Zhao She’s occupation of Beishan, whereas Cao Man’s encampment at Wulin brought him into peril! Yin and yang deserve esteem, yet some have met defeat on a jiazi day, while others have risen to success on a day designated “going forth to destruction.” Technical skill must be employed, yet some, adopting chariot warfare, gained access to the states of the central realm, while others, employing chariot warfare, brought the royal army to ruin. As the saying goes, some employ these methods and lose, while others employ them and win. Must the fault not lie in how the methods are applied?

In the Han we find a Marquis of Martial Prowess, who marched west out of Qishan without looking back, and captured Meng Huo in the south without putting him to death…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江武舉鄉試錄
text:
畏蜀如虎而身後猶稱爲天下奇才者蓋
武侯八陣本六韜而其節制則司馬法之
遺也故四事四術之用極天下之至深於
宋得一武穆焉内破虔吉之劇盜外抗兀
术之强胡用兵如神至有望其旌旗而不
敢近者蓋武穆節制得司馬而其運用則
亦六韜之法也故四事四術之用極天下
之至變武穆曰運用之妙存乎一心武侯
===
曰用兵之道攻心爲上斯又二公心術之
妙而折衝禦侮之要誠有出於兵法之外
者向使吾心一泥其法則奇正誤用攻守
皆非權謀形勢陰陽技巧不用敗也用亦
敗也以此而語兵法則亦讀父書之流耳
故談兵愈詳而所以制敵者愈踈也嗟乎
兵者氣也夫志氣之帥也武侯亦隆中之
一匹夫也感三顧之勤而許以馳驅武穆
punctuated:
畏蜀如虎，而身後猶稱爲天下奇才者，蓋武侯八陣本六韜，而其節制則司馬法之遺也。故四事四術之用，極天下之至深。於宋得一武穆焉，内破虔吉之劇盜，外抗兀术之强胡，用兵如神，至有望其旌旗而不敢近者。蓋武穆節制得司馬，而其運用則亦六韜之法也。故四事四術之用，極天下之至變。武穆曰：「運用之妙，存乎一心。」武侯曰：「用兵之道，攻心爲上。」斯又二公心術之妙，而折衝禦侮之要，誠有出於兵法之外者。
向使吾心一泥其法，則奇正誤用，攻守皆非。權謀、形勢、陰陽、技巧，不用敗也，用亦敗也。以此而語兵法，則亦讀父書之流耳。故談兵愈詳，而所以制敵者愈踈也。
嗟乎！兵者，氣也。夫志，氣之帥也。武侯亦隆中之一匹夫也，感三顧之勤而許以馳驅。武穆
translation_en:
…they feared Shu as they would a tiger, and even after his death he was still acclaimed as an extraordinary talent without equal under Heaven. This was because the Eight Formations of the Martial Marquis, Zhuge Liang, were based on the Six Secret Teachings, while his military discipline inherited the Methods of Sima. Thus his use of the four matters and four arts reached the utmost depths attainable under Heaven. In the Song there was a Lord Wumu, Yue Fei. Within the realm he crushed the formidable bandits of Qian and Ji; against external foes he resisted Wuzhu’s powerful northern forces. His handling of troops was divinely inspired, so much so that some who saw his banners dared not approach. Wumu’s military discipline derived from the Methods of Sima, while his practical deployment likewise followed the methods of the Six Secret Teachings. Thus his use of the four matters and four arts attained the utmost adaptability under Heaven. Wumu said, “The subtlety of applying them lies in the mind alone.” The Martial Marquis said, “In warfare, attacking the heart is best.” Here, too, lay the subtlety of these two men’s mastery of the mind and the essentials of repelling enemies and resisting aggression: these truly extended beyond the written methods of warfare.
If we were to let our minds cling rigidly to those methods, we would misuse both unorthodox and orthodox operations, and err alike in attack and defence. Strategic planning, configurations of force, yin and yang, and technical skills: without using them we would fail, yet using them we would also fail. To discuss military methods in this way is merely to belong among those who read their fathers’ books. Thus, the more minutely they discuss warfare, the less adequate their means of overcoming the enemy become.
Alas! Warfare depends on vital spirit, and resolve is the commander of that spirit. The Martial Marquis, too, was once an ordinary man of Longzhong. Moved by the earnestness of the three visits, he pledged himself to devoted service. Wumu…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江武舉鄉試錄
text:
始好野戰未必盡謀於法者憫二帝之蒙
塵而獨思爲討賊之計故其言曰竭以股
肱之力死而後巳彼與唾手燕雲矢心天
地之蹤若後先一律而可以貫金石動鬼
神者忠義一倡何兵心之不可感而兵法
之不可精耶此謂作用之本也夫枕戈報
胡請纓繫越者不必借才而後有之也而
于今南北爲雲亂畧未遏若未盡舒其憤
之氣者何也忠義之志猶有所未立也
===
又
朱天相
馬上中七箭
步下中四箭
古之謀臣將士所以相君圖治而功業有
不同者君子尚論其心而巳心也者致用
之本也心之公私少異而治効之隆汚頓
punctuated:
始好野戰，未必盡謀於法者，憫二帝之蒙塵，而獨思爲討賊之計。故其言曰：「竭以股肱之力，死而後巳。」彼與唾手燕雲、矢心天地之蹤，若後先一律，而可以貫金石、動鬼神者，忠義一倡，何兵心之不可感，而兵法之不可精耶？此謂作用之本也。夫枕戈報胡、請纓繫越者，不必借才而後有之也。而于今南北爲雲，亂畧未遏，若未盡舒其憤之氣者，何也？忠義之志猶有所未立也。

又
朱天相
馬上中七箭，步下中四箭。

古之謀臣將士，所以相君圖治而功業有不同者，君子尚論其心而巳。心也者，致用之本也。心之公私少異，而治効之隆汚頓
translation_en:
…at first favored fighting in the open field and did not necessarily base all his plans on established methods. Grieving that the two emperors had been driven into captivity, he thought only of plans to punish the rebels. Hence the words: “I shall exhaust my strength in service, ceasing only at death.” His deeds and those of the man who vowed before Heaven and Earth to recover Yan and Yun with ease followed the same pattern, though one came before the other. Their resolve could pierce metal and stone and move ghosts and spirits. Once loyalty and righteousness are championed, what soldiers’ hearts cannot be stirred, and what military methods cannot be mastered? This is what is meant by the foundation of effective action. Those who sleep with their heads upon their weapons to take vengeance on the Hu [?], or request a cord with which to bind the ruler of Yue, need not await borrowed talent before such resolve can arise. Yet today, in north and south, troubles gather like clouds [?], and disorder and depredation remain unchecked. Why does it seem that their indignant spirit has not been fully given vent? Because their commitment to loyalty and righteousness is still not firmly established.

Another model answer
Zhu Tianxiang hit the target with seven arrows on horseback and four arrows on foot.

As for why the strategists and military men of antiquity differed in their achievements when assisting their rulers and pursuing good government, the gentleman, in appraising them, considers only their hearts. The heart is the foundation of effective action. The slightest difference between public-mindedness and selfishness in the heart abruptly makes the results of government greater or poorer…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江武舉鄉試錄
text:
殊心之運量不同而事功之成敗遂別故
善事君者必當以天德王道爲本而不可
秉之以急功謀利之私善將兵者必當以
興王定亂爲期而不可先之以成敗利鈍
之念夫然後可以奏安攘之大功收平定
之偉績而志之所向力之所加將無往而
不遂矣否則狃於功利之私者其所就必
不大急於身家之務者其爲謀必不忠亦
何以盡輔相之職而樹勲名於天下後世
也哉
===
執事三策武士而以古謀臣將士爲問其所
以望諸生者不淺也敢不摭所聞以對今
夫先王制弧矢以威天下除戎器以戒不
虞兵固治世之所諱言而亦有國者之不
容不講也考之周官大司馬掌九伐之法
以正邦國因井田以寓軍政其經常簡易
punctuated:
殊。心之運量不同，而事功之成敗遂別。故善事君者，必當以天德王道爲本，而不可秉之以急功謀利之私；善將兵者，必當以興王定亂爲期，而不可先之以成敗利鈍之念。夫然後可以奏安攘之大功，收平定之偉績，而志之所向、力之所加，將無往而不遂矣。否則，狃於功利之私者，其所就必不大；急於身家之務者，其爲謀必不忠。亦何以盡輔相之職，而樹勲名於天下後世也哉？

執事三策武士，而以古謀臣將士爲問，其所以望諸生者不淺也。敢不摭所聞以對？今夫先王制弧矢以威天下，除戎器以戒不虞。兵固治世之所諱言，而亦有國者之不容不講也。考之《周官》，大司馬掌九伐之法，以正邦國；因井田以寓軍政，其經常簡易
translation_en:
…differ markedly. When the mind’s deliberations differ, success and failure in undertakings consequently diverge. Thus, those who serve their ruler well must take Heaven’s virtue and the kingly Way as their foundation, rather than act from selfish desires for quick achievements and personal gain. Those who command troops well must make the flourishing of kingship and the suppression of disorder their aim, rather than give precedence to considerations of success or failure, advantage or adversity. Only then can they accomplish the great work of securing peace within and repelling threats from without, and achieve the splendid feat of pacification. Wherever their resolve is directed and their strength applied, nothing will fail to be accomplished. Otherwise, those habituated to selfish pursuits of achievement and profit will necessarily accomplish little; those preoccupied with their own persons and households will necessarily be disloyal in their counsels. How could they then fulfill their duties as the ruler’s assistants and establish meritorious reputations throughout the realm and for later generations?

You, honored examiners, have posed three policy questions to military candidates, asking about the counselors and military officers of antiquity. Your expectations of us candidates are far from slight. How could I dare not draw upon what I have learned in reply? The former kings fashioned bows and arrows to overawe all under Heaven, and put weapons in readiness against unforeseen dangers. Military matters are admittedly a subject people avoid discussing in an age of good government, yet they are also something no ruler of a state can neglect to study. Examining the Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan), we find that the Grand Marshal administered the rules for nine types of punitive expedition in order to rectify the states. Military administration was incorporated into the well-field system, and its regular, simple …

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江武舉鄉試錄
text:
之制粲然大備兹固王道之紀也後有作
者舉而行之治功不足言矣夫何管仲之
相齊桓也取周官之法而變其說作內政
於國中以寓兵作鄙制於國外以寓農昔
無兵農之分也自夷吾變之而兵農始分
矣是周官之法固爲王道之紀然時至春
秋王綱廢墜管氏以急功之心而加之以
淺陿之量故九合一匡之功僅足以挽王
===
室之衰耳功之所以止於霸者豈周官之
法有所遷就也哉孔子之賛夷吾曰一匡
天下管仲之力也如其仁如其仁蓋有取
其尊周攘夷之績耳太公之著兵法象八
卦以立六韜隨六韜以申三畧其參伍變
化之機莫可窺測兹固兵家之範也後有
作者倣而用之勳業自烜赫矣夫何張良
之佐漢也持韜畧之法以說沛公運籌帷
punctuated:
之制粲然大備，兹固王道之紀也。後有作者舉而行之，治功不足言矣。夫何管仲之相齊桓也，取周官之法而變其說，作內政於國中以寓兵，作鄙制於國外以寓農。昔無兵農之分也，自夷吾變之而兵農始分矣。是周官之法固爲王道之紀，然時至春秋，王綱廢墜，管氏以急功之心而加之以淺陿之量，故九合一匡之功僅足以挽王室之衰耳。功之所以止於霸者，豈周官之法有所遷就也哉？孔子之賛夷吾曰：「一匡天下，管仲之力也。如其仁！如其仁！」蓋有取其尊周攘夷之績耳。

太公之著兵法，象八卦以立六韜，隨六韜以申三畧，其參伍變化之機莫可窺測，兹固兵家之範也。後有作者倣而用之，勳業自烜赫矣。夫何張良之佐漢也，持韜畧之法以說沛公，運籌帷
translation_en:
…its enduring and straightforward institutions were splendidly complete. These were indeed the guiding principles of the kingly Way. Had later men arisen to put them into practice, their achievements in government would have been beyond description. Why, then, did Guan Zhong, when serving as chief minister to Duke Huan of Qi, take the methods of the Offices of Zhou and alter their interpretation, establishing an internal administration within the capital to incorporate military organization and a system of rural districts outside it to incorporate agriculture? Previously, soldiers and farmers had not been separate; only after Yiwu—that is, Guan Zhong—changed the system did the two become distinct. Thus, although the methods of the Offices of Zhou were indeed the guiding principles of the kingly Way, by the Spring and Autumn period the royal order had fallen into ruin. Guan combined an eagerness for quick results with a narrow capacity of mind. Consequently, his achievements in convening the lords nine times and setting the realm right sufficed only to check the decline of the royal house. Could the fact that his achievements went no further than those of a hegemon have resulted from any compromise inherent in the methods of the Offices of Zhou? Confucius praised Yiwu, saying: “That the realm was set right was due to Guan Zhong’s efforts. Such was his benevolence! Such was his benevolence!” He was surely commending only Guan’s accomplishments in honoring Zhou and repelling the barbarians.

When the Grand Duke composed his military teachings, he modeled the Six Secret Teachings on the Eight Trigrams and followed the Six Secret Teachings with the Three Strategies to elaborate them. The workings of their combinations and transformations were beyond fathoming. These were indeed models for military strategists. Had later men arisen to follow and employ them, their achievements would naturally have been illustrious. Why, then, did Zhang Liang, when assisting the Han, use the methods of the Six Secret Teachings and Three Strategies to counsel the Duke of Pei, devising plans within the curtains…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江武舉鄉試錄
text:
幄之中決勝千里之外黃石丹書之祕傳
之圯上而施爲運量先儒稱其有儒者氣
象矣夫太公之制固爲兵家之範然時當
秦季風會澆漓子房挾報復之私而因之
以馬上之習故爲韓翼漢之志僅足以成
雜覇之業爾用之所以不多見者豈非韜
光而不露也哉邵子之稱良曰智哉留侯
善藏其用蓋有取其明哲保身之機耳夫
===
兵法四事有奇有正有攻有守正所以設
險也奇所以取勝也攻所以懾敵也守所
以觀變也故用兵之道莫善於用正莫不
善於用奇莫强於能攻莫不强於能守然
自奇正而觀有宜於正有不宜於正者有
可用奇有不可用奇者自攻守而觀有必
於攻有不必於攻者有利於守有不利於
守者兵志曰凡戰之道衆寡以觀其變進
punctuated:
幄之中，決勝千里之外。黃石丹書之祕，傳之圯上，而施爲運量，先儒稱其有儒者氣象矣。夫太公之制，固爲兵家之範，然時當秦季，風會澆漓，子房挾報復之私，而因之以馬上之習，故爲韓翼漢之志，僅足以成雜覇之業爾。用之所以不多見者，豈非韜光而不露也哉？邵子之稱良曰：「智哉留侯，善藏其用。」蓋有取其明哲保身之機耳。
夫兵法四事，有奇有正，有攻有守。正所以設險也，奇所以取勝也，攻所以懾敵也，守所以觀變也。故用兵之道，莫善於用正，莫不善於用奇，莫强於能攻，莫不强於能守。然自奇正而觀，有宜於正、有不宜於正者，有可用奇、有不可用奇者；自攻守而觀，有必於攻、有不必於攻者，有利於守、有不利於守者。《兵志》曰：「凡戰之道，衆寡以觀其變，進
translation_en:
…within the command tent, deciding victory a thousand li away. The secrets of Huangshi’s Vermilion Writ were transmitted to him upon the bridge; in his actions and calculations, earlier Confucian scholars discerned the bearing of a Confucian. The methods established by Taigong were indeed a model for military strategists. Yet this was the closing age of Qin, when prevailing customs had become shallow and corrupt. Zifang [Zhang Liang] harbored a private desire for vengeance and coupled it with the habits of warfare on horseback. Thus his ambition to assist Han 漢 for the sake of Han 韓 sufficed only to establish a hegemony of mixed character. Was the infrequent manifestation of his abilities not due to his concealing his brilliance rather than displaying it? Master Shao praised Liang, saying: “Wise indeed was the Marquis of Liu, skilled at concealing his abilities.” What he valued was Liang’s capacity to preserve himself through discerning wisdom.
Military methods comprise four matters: the unorthodox and the orthodox, attack and defense. Orthodox methods establish defensive obstacles; unorthodox methods secure victory; attack intimidates the enemy; defense allows one to observe changes. Thus, in the conduct of war, nothing is better than employing orthodox methods, nothing worse than employing unorthodox methods, nothing stronger than the ability to attack, and nothing weaker than the ability to defend. Yet, considering orthodox and unorthodox methods, there are circumstances suited to orthodox methods and circumstances unsuited to them, occasions when unorthodox methods may be used and occasions when they may not. Considering attack and defense, there are circumstances requiring attack and circumstances not requiring it, circumstances favorable to defense and circumstances unfavorable to it. The Military Records states: “In the general conduct of battle, use numerical superiority and inferiority to observe the enemy’s responses to change; advance …

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江武舉鄉試錄
text:
退以觀其固危而觀其懼靜而觀其怠動
而觀其疑襲而觀其治由是言之烏可以
一定拘哉或者乃謂其正無別攻守一道
固矣豈知趙括能讀父書不免長平之敗
張巡不傚古法獨守睢陽之城亞夫知崤
澠之路不可由而藍田一走七國之功成
矣何馬援矍鑠之勇不免五溪之敗耶曹
公知華費之城不可攻而徐州一入三分
===
之業定矣何沈攸老練之才不免全軍之
覆耶是皆古人已行之事而成敗之或異
者法之不可窮也兵家有四術曰權謀曰
形勢曰陰陽曰技巧權謀所以運機智也
形勢所以審地利也陰陽所以驗天時也
技巧所以精武畧也用兵之道匪得天時
則弗順匪得地利則弗據匪機智則謀弗
神匪武畧則戰弗勝自發策制勝而言惟
punctuated:
退以觀其固，危而觀其懼，靜而觀其怠，動而觀其疑，襲而觀其治。」由是言之，烏可以一定拘哉？或者乃謂其正無別，攻守一道，固矣！豈知趙括能讀父書，不免長平之敗；張巡不傚古法，獨守睢陽之城；亞夫知崤澠之路不可由，而藍田一走，七國之功成矣。何馬援矍鑠之勇，不免五溪之敗耶？曹公知華費之城不可攻，而徐州一入，三分之業定矣。何沈攸老練之才，不免全軍之覆耶？是皆古人已行之事，而成敗之或異者，法之不可窮也。
兵家有四術，曰權謀，曰形勢，曰陰陽，曰技巧。權謀所以運機智也，形勢所以審地利也，陰陽所以驗天時也，技巧所以精武畧也。用兵之道，匪得天時則弗順，匪得地利則弗據，匪機智則謀弗神，匪武畧則戰弗勝。自發策制勝而言，惟
translation_en:
…retreat to observe their firmness; endanger them to observe their fear; remain still to observe their negligence; move to observe their uncertainty; launch a surprise attack to observe their discipline.” In light of this, how could one be constrained by a single fixed rule? Some nevertheless maintain that regular dispositions admit no distinctions [?], and that attack and defense follow a single course. How inflexible! Do they not know that Zhao Kuo could read his father’s military writings, yet could not escape defeat at Changping; that Zhang Xun did not imitate ancient methods, yet single-handedly defended the city of Suiyang; and that Yafu knew the route through Xiao and Mian could not be taken, but by a single march through Lantian accomplished the defeat of the Seven Kingdoms [?]? Why, then, did Ma Yuan, for all his vigor and courage, fail to escape defeat at Wuxi? Lord Cao knew that the city of Huafei [?] could not be attacked, yet by entering Xuzhou once established the foundation of his share in the tripartite division of the realm. Why, then, did Shen You [?], for all his seasoned ability, fail to prevent the destruction of his entire army? These are all deeds performed by men of antiquity. Their differing outcomes—success or failure—show that the possibilities of military methods cannot be exhausted.
Military specialists have four arts: strategic planning, dispositions and configurations, yin and yang, and technical skills. Strategic planning employs resourcefulness; dispositions and configurations assess the advantages of terrain; yin and yang examine favorable timing in Heaven’s cycles; and technical skills refine military prowess. In conducting war, without favorable timing, operations will not proceed smoothly; without favorable terrain, there will be no secure position; without resourcefulness, plans will lack inspired ingenuity; and without military prowess, battles will not be won. As for devising plans and securing victory, only…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江武舉鄉試錄
text:
智謀之深斯可以臨機而應變惟技巧之
精斯可折衝而禦侮自權敵樹勲而觀惟
天時之善斯可以奮勇而克捷惟地利之
固斯可以乘亂而擣虛兵志曰兵詭道也
能而示之不能用而示之不用近而示之
遠遠而示之近攻其無備出其不意即是
觀之烏可以一律齊哉或者有見於用之
古今或以取勝或以致敗遂謂兵法之不
足信固矣豈知田單以一卒爲神遂著收
燕之績而郭京六甲之作竟爲楚師所敗
天時何足秉耶趙奢據北山而戰克奏取
秦之功而劉備馬鞍之據卒爲陸遜所蹙
地利何足倚耶智氏以韓魏之兵伐趙而
晉陽以潰廉頗率老幼之卒守邯鄲而栗
腹以摧是不在權謀之多寡也以東晉之
衰而謝玄得志於淝水以後秦之衆而符
punctuated: 智謀之深，斯可以臨機而應變；惟技巧之精，斯可折衝而禦侮。自權敵樹勲而觀，惟天時之善，斯可以奮勇而克捷；惟地利之固，斯可以乘亂而擣虛。《兵志》曰：「兵，詭道也。能而示之不能，用而示之不用，近而示之遠，遠而示之近，攻其無備，出其不意。」即是觀之，烏可以一律齊哉？或者有見於用之古今，或以取勝，或以致敗，遂謂兵法之不足信，固矣。豈知田單以一卒爲神，遂著收燕之績，而郭京六甲之作，竟爲楚師所敗，天時何足秉耶？趙奢據北山而戰，克奏取秦之功，而劉備馬鞍之據，卒爲陸遜所蹙，地利何足倚耶？智氏以韓魏之兵伐趙，而晉陽以潰；廉頗率老幼之卒守邯鄲，而栗腹以摧，是不在權謀之多寡也。以東晉之衰，而謝玄得志於淝水；以後秦之衆，而符
translation_en:
…only with profound strategic wisdom can one respond to changing circumstances as they arise; only with refined military skills can one repel assaults and resist aggression. Viewed in terms of weighing the enemy’s strength and establishing merit, only favorable celestial timing enables one to fight courageously and achieve victory; only a secure advantage of terrain enables one to exploit disorder and strike at weak points. The Military Records states: “Warfare is the way of deception. When capable, appear incapable; when employing your forces, appear not to employ them; when near, appear far away; when far away, appear near. Attack where the enemy is unprepared; emerge where he does not expect you.” Viewed thus, how could warfare be governed uniformly by a single rule?

Some observe that, in ancient and modern times, applying military methods has sometimes brought victory and sometimes defeat, and consequently declare those methods unworthy of trust. This is surely a blinkered view. Do they not know that Tian Dan treated a single soldier as divine [?] and thereby achieved distinction in recovering territory from Yan, whereas Guo Jing’s deployment of the Six Jia spirits ultimately suffered defeat at the hands of the army of Chu [?]? How, then, could celestial timing alone be sufficient to rely upon? Zhao She occupied Beishan and fought, successfully defeating Qin; yet Liu Bei’s occupation of Ma’an ultimately left him hard pressed by Lu Xun. How, then, could advantageous terrain alone be sufficient to rely upon?

The Zhi clan attacked Zhao with the armies of Han and Wei, yet its forces collapsed at Jinyang; Lian Po led troops composed of old men and youths in defending Handan, yet Li Fu was crushed. Thus the outcome does not depend on the quantity of stratagems. Despite the weakness of Eastern Jin, Xie Xuan achieved his aim at Feishui; despite the multitude of Later Qin’s troops [?], Fu…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江武舉鄉試錄
text:
堅投鞭於公山是不在技巧之淺深也此
皆古人已試之迹而成敗有不同者機之
不可測也易曰化而裁之存乎變推而行
之存乎通神而明之存乎其人其此之謂
乎歷考古之將士其所賦之才質不同而
所施之經畧亦異有謀將有智將有勇將
而其以儒將稱者乃獨有取於漢之武侯
宋之武穆焉吾觀武侯定軍制立八陣之
===
法擊首則尾應擊尾則首應擊中則首尾
俱應故臨敵決戰電掣雷奔擒孟獲於瀘
南走曹瞞於赤壁鼎足三分興復漢室先
儒稱孔明有儒者氣象豈非以其心之正
而不譎乎武穆好野戰不閑兵畧妙用存
乎一心惟在兵識將意將識士情使人各
自爲戰故操縱開闔鬼没神輸提戈捲燕
雲之塵長驅破賀蘭之缺誓復山河幾還
punctuated: 堅投鞭於公山，是不在技巧之淺深也。此皆古人已試之迹，而成敗有不同者，機之不可測也。《易》曰：「化而裁之存乎變，推而行之存乎通，神而明之存乎其人。」其此之謂乎？歷考古之將士，其所賦之才質不同，而所施之經畧亦異。有謀將，有智將，有勇將，而其以儒將稱者，乃獨有取於漢之武侯、宋之武穆焉。吾觀武侯定軍制，立八陣之法，擊首則尾應，擊尾則首應，擊中則首尾俱應。故臨敵決戰，電掣雷奔，擒孟獲於瀘南，走曹瞞於赤壁，鼎足三分，興復漢室。先儒稱孔明有儒者氣象，豈非以其心之正而不譎乎？武穆好野戰，不閑兵畧，妙用存乎一心，惟在兵識將意，將識士情，使人各自爲戰。故操縱開闔，鬼没神輸，提戈捲燕雲之塵，長驅破賀蘭之缺，誓復山河，幾還
translation_en:
…Jian [Fu Jian, whose surname begins on the preceding page] cast his whip at Gongshan [?]: this shows that the outcome did not depend on the degree of technical skill. These are all precedents tested by men of antiquity; their differing successes and failures arose from the unpredictability of circumstances. The Book of Changes says: “Transforming and shaping things depends on change; extending them and putting them into practice depends on free passage; making them wondrous and illuminating them depends on the person.” Is this not what it means?

Surveying the generals and soldiers of antiquity, we find that their natural talents differed, as did the strategies they employed. There were generals of planning, generals of wisdom, and generals of courage. Yet among those called Confucian generals, particular esteem is reserved for the Martial Marquis of Han [Zhuge Liang] and Wumu of Song [Yue Fei]. I observe that the Martial Marquis established military organization and instituted the method of the Eight Formations: when the head was attacked, the tail responded; when the tail was attacked, the head responded; when the center was attacked, head and tail responded together. Thus, when facing the enemy in decisive battle, he moved like flashing lightning and rushing thunder. He captured Meng Huo south of the Lu River and drove Cao Man [Cao Cao] into flight at Chibi, establishing one of three powers like the legs of a tripod and reviving the house of Han. Earlier Confucian scholars praised Kongming [Zhuge Liang] for possessing the bearing of a Confucian. Was this not because his heart was upright and without deceit?

Wumu favored battle in the open field and was not versed in military strategy [?]. His marvelous application of military methods resided entirely in his own mind: the essential thing was for soldiers to understand their commander's intentions and for the commander to understand his men's feelings, so that each man would fight on his own initiative. Thus, in holding back and releasing, opening and closing his formations, he vanished like a ghost and moved like a spirit [?]. Raising his spear, he swept away the dust of war from Yan and Yun; driving far forward, he broke through the gaps of Helan. He vowed to recover the realm and almost brought back…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江武舉鄉試錄
text:
二聖先正謂岳飛有仁者之勇豈非以其
心之忠而不貳乎夫用兵貴乎有紀尚節
制也決勝期於無形尚權變也二者兵家
之大防也若二公者誠爲獨得之深矣然
豈無所本乎太公之六韜多變法巳極權
謀之深而武侯八陣之圖則固本六韜而
充焉者也左氏之論兵多古法尚近節制
之師而武穆料理之精則又本左氏而神
===
焉者也又豈無所合乎武侯八陣雖本六
韜而其節制之詳則又得諸左氏故其兵
之用也極天下之至神岳飛兵法雖本左
氏而其運動之奇則又得諸六韜故其師
之行也極天下之至變是蓋武侯之將兵
純任法而持之以心武穆之將兵純任心
而參之以法要皆本於心術之正而功之
成敗利鈍則非二子所能必也要而論之
punctuated: 二聖。先正謂岳飛有仁者之勇，豈非以其心之忠而不貳乎？夫用兵貴乎有紀，尚節制也；決勝期於無形，尚權變也。二者，兵家之大防也。若二公者，誠爲獨得之深矣。然豈無所本乎？太公之《六韜》多變法，巳極權謀之深，而武侯八陣之圖，則固本《六韜》而充焉者也。左氏之論兵多古法，尚近節制之師，而武穆料理之精，則又本左氏而神焉者也。又豈無所合乎？武侯八陣雖本《六韜》，而其節制之詳，則又得諸左氏，故其兵之用也，極天下之至神。岳飛兵法雖本左氏，而其運動之奇，則又得諸《六韜》，故其師之行也，極天下之至變。是蓋武侯之將兵，純任法而持之以心；武穆之將兵，純任心而參之以法。要皆本於心術之正，而功之成敗利鈍，則非二子所能必也。要而論之，
translation_en:
…the two emperors. An earlier worthy said that Yue Fei possessed the courage of a benevolent man. Was this not because his heart was loyal and undivided? In employing troops, one prizes order: this means valuing discipline and control. In securing victory, one seeks to leave no discernible form: this means valuing expedient adaptation. These two are the great safeguards of military practice. Men such as these two masters truly attained an exceptionally profound understanding of them. Yet did they have no foundation to draw upon? The Grand Duke’s Six Secret Teachings (Liu tao) contains many methods of adaptation and already plumbs the depths of strategic calculation. Marquis Wu’s diagram of the Eight Formations was firmly grounded in the Six Secret Teachings and developed it further. Master Zuo’s discussions of warfare contain many ancient methods and remain close to the ideal of an army governed by discipline and control. Wumu’s mastery of military management likewise drew upon Master Zuo and brought his teachings to a wondrous level.

Moreover, did they not also combine these traditions? Although Marquis Wu’s Eight Formations were grounded in the Six Secret Teachings, the detailed provisions for discipline and control were also drawn from Master Zuo. Thus his employment of troops reached the utmost heights of wondrous skill. Although Yue Fei’s military methods were grounded in Master Zuo, his extraordinary maneuvers were also drawn from the Six Secret Teachings. Thus the movements of his army reached the utmost heights of adaptability. In commanding troops, Marquis Wu relied wholly upon established methods, governing them through his mind; Wumu relied wholly upon his mind, supplementing it with established methods. In essence, both were grounded in upright intentions. Whether their endeavors succeeded or failed, and whether circumstances favored or hindered them, were things neither man could guarantee. To sum up the argument, …

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江武舉鄉試錄
text:
周官之法度王道之中正也太公之韜畧
王制之緒餘也管仲以急功之心故僅能
成一匡之績子房尚黄老之術此漢治所
以終流於雜覇也觀咢足之勢者尚武侯
之奇而惜其功之不就慨南冠之縶者壯
武穆之烈而痛其志之不終也蓋凡逞功
利之私則無以成光大之業事奇譎之術
則無以奏膚碩之功惟忠以立心正以持
節其幸而功之成耶天也不幸而捐軀以
報國亦天也君子盡其在我者而已矣然
則事君者烏可不審所尚而觀人者又烏
可以成敗論英雄哉我
===
國家稽古定制選將掄材所用皆周官太公
之方畧所將皆武侯武穆之忠貞雍熈累
洽二百年於兹矣馴至今日士多虚談兵
皆玩愒足蹈軍門者六韜尚昧育戴武弁
punctuated: 周官之法度，王道之中正也；太公之韜畧，王制之緒餘也。管仲以急功之心，故僅能成一匡之績；子房尚黄老之術，此漢治所以終流於雜覇也。觀咢足之勢者，尚武侯之奇，而惜其功之不就；慨南冠之縶者，壯武穆之烈，而痛其志之不終也。蓋凡逞功利之私，則無以成光大之業；事奇譎之術，則無以奏膚碩之功。惟忠以立心，正以持節，其幸而功之成耶，天也；不幸而捐軀以報國，亦天也。君子盡其在我者而已矣。然則事君者，烏可不審所尚，而觀人者，又烏可以成敗論英雄哉？我國家稽古定制，選將掄材，所用皆周官、太公之方畧，所將皆武侯、武穆之忠貞，雍熈累洽二百年於兹矣。馴至今日，士多虚談，兵皆玩愒。足蹈軍門者，六韜尚昧；育戴武弁
translation_en:
…The laws and institutions of the Offices of Zhou embody the balance and rectitude of the kingly Way; the military strategies of Taigong are the surviving legacy of royal institutions. Guan Zhong, intent on rapid achievement, could accomplish only the feat of setting the realm in order. Zifang esteemed the arts of Huangdi and Laozi; this is why Han government ultimately lapsed into a mixture incorporating hegemonic rule. Those who contemplate the configuration of contending powers [?] admire the extraordinary abilities of Marquis Wu, yet regret that his undertaking remained unfulfilled. Those who lament the bonds of the southern captive admire the heroic deeds of Wumu, yet grieve that his aspirations were never fully realized.

Those who indulge private desires for achievement and advantage have no means of establishing a great and illustrious undertaking; those who pursue extraordinary and deceptive arts have no means of achieving substantial accomplishments. Only loyalty should establish one’s intentions, and rectitude sustain one’s integrity. If one is fortunate enough to succeed, that is Heaven; if, through misfortune, one sacrifices one’s life to repay the state, that too is Heaven. The gentleman merely does all that lies within his own power. How, then, can one who serves a ruler fail to scrutinize what he esteems? And how can one who assesses others judge heroes by success or failure?

Our dynasty has examined antiquity to establish its institutions, selecting commanders and choosing men of talent. The strategies it employs are all those of the Offices of Zhou and Taigong; its commanders possess the loyalty and steadfastness of Marquis Wu and Wumu. Harmony and prosperity have accumulated for two hundred years down to the present. Yet gradually we have reached a day when men largely indulge in empty talk, and soldiers all idle away their time. Those who set foot within military headquarters remain ignorant even of the Six Secret Teachings; those who [?] wear military caps…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江武舉鄉試錄
text:
者左氏未聞以是而欲從事於軍旅之中
祗見其安馬而已安望其能戰勝攻取以
成天下之事哉要必使言兵者如周官之
詳而盡六韜之智而深左氏之約而大用
兵者如張良之謀而隱武侯之深而安武
穆之神而變則推演陣法極深研幾騎步
相參五兵互用可以盡天下之變矣閱練
精熟窺敵伺變疾莫可知奇莫能測可以
盡天下之神矣何兵威之不可強盛邊鄙
之不可肅清哉愚悉何幸躬逢其盛
===
論
大明發而萬物皆照
毛　詩
馬上中六箭
步下中五箭
王者厲武以定傾非意而爲之也所以蕩滌稜
punctuated:
者，左氏未聞。以是而欲從事於軍旅之中，祗見其安馬而已，安望其能戰勝攻取，以成天下之事哉？要必使言兵者如周官之詳而盡、六韜之智而深、左氏之約而大；用兵者如張良之謀而隱、武侯之深而安、武穆之神而變。則推演陣法，極深研幾，騎步相參，五兵互用，可以盡天下之變矣。閱練精熟，窺敵伺變，疾莫可知，奇莫能測，可以盡天下之神矣。何兵威之不可強盛、邊鄙之不可肅清哉？愚悉何幸，躬逢其盛！

論
大明發而萬物皆照。
毛　詩
馬上中六箭，步下中五箭。

王者厲武以定傾，非意而爲之也，所以蕩滌稜
translation_en:
…have never heard of the Zuo Tradition. If such men wish to undertake military service, we shall see only their settling horses [?]; how can we expect them to win battles and capture objectives, thereby accomplishing the affairs of the realm? Those who discuss warfare must possess the detail and comprehensiveness of the Offices of Zhou, the wisdom and depth of the Six Secret Teachings, and the concision and breadth of the Zuo Tradition. Those who conduct warfare must possess Zhang Liang’s concealed strategic designs, the depth and steadiness of the Marquis of Wu [Zhuge Liang], and the marvelous adaptability of Wumu [Yue Fei]. Then, by developing battle formations, plumbing their depths and investigating the first stirrings of change, coordinating cavalry and infantry, and employing the five kinds of weapons in conjunction, they can encompass every possible transformation under Heaven. Through thorough inspection and training, watching the enemy and awaiting changes, with speed that none can fathom and surprise tactics that none can predict, they can exhaust warfare’s marvelous possibilities. How could military might fail to flourish, or the borderlands fail to be pacified? How fortunate I am [?] to witness such flourishing in person!

Discourse
“When the Great Light Emerges, All Things Are Illuminated”
Mao Shi.

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江武舉鄉試錄
text:
氣而曠然與天下清明也其諸天之有日乎衆
陽融結而大明生焉覆露照導而無私者也王
者之師象是矣夫天下之大無垠也天下之人
之衆何限也吾以智先天下則天下以智應我
而溯不可測吾以力鬭天下則天下以力角我
而兢不勝舉且將紛紛籍籍與吾爭一旦之命
而吾以一人服之豈徒恃兵而足哉故王者之
用兵也抵釁而動俟時而發其所以討暴除穢
===
以廓清四海者蓋誠通於本而無事於末觀於
要而不惑於詳也人見王者制兵有法或以爲
整齊天下之具在是矣而不知非其本要也昔
人謂法生於義義生於衆適衆適合於人心斯
得之矣世傳六韜爲太公所著吾雖未敢盡信
之也乃其告文王曰大明發而萬物皆照大義
發而萬物皆利大兵發而萬物皆服豈不誠然
言哉吾嘗觀乎天文而徵諸載籍矣日之爲耀
punctuated: 氣，而曠然與天下清明也。其諸天之有日乎？衆陽融結而大明生焉，覆露照導而無私者也。王者之師象是矣。夫天下之大無垠也，天下之人之衆何限也！吾以智先天下，則天下以智應我，而溯不可測；吾以力鬭天下，則天下以力角我，而兢不勝舉。且將紛紛籍籍，與吾爭一旦之命，而吾以一人服之，豈徒恃兵而足哉？故王者之用兵也，抵釁而動，俟時而發。其所以討暴除穢，以廓清四海者，蓋誠通於本而無事於末，觀於要而不惑於詳也。人見王者制兵有法，或以爲整齊天下之具在是矣，而不知非其本要也。昔人謂：「法生於義，義生於衆適，衆適合於人心。」斯得之矣。世傳《六韜》爲太公所著，吾雖未敢盡信之也，乃其告文王曰：「大明發而萬物皆照，大義發而萬物皆利，大兵發而萬物皆服。」豈不誠然言哉？吾嘗觀乎天文而徵諸載籍矣。日之爲耀
translation_en: … malign force, and thereby bring expansive clarity and peace to all under Heaven. Is this not like Heaven’s having the sun? The manifold forces of yang fuse and coalesce, and the great light comes into being, impartially sheltering, nourishing, illuminating, and guiding. The army of a true king takes this as its model. The world is boundless in its extent, and how could its people be numbered! If I seek to outwit all under Heaven, they will answer me with their own cleverness, whose workings cannot be fathomed [?]; if I contend with all under Heaven through force, they will pit their strength against mine, and the rivalries will be too numerous to enumerate. Moreover, in their tumultuous multitudes they will contend with me for their very lives on a single day. If I, one man, am to subdue them, how could reliance on arms alone suffice? Thus, when a true king employs troops, he moves when an opening presents itself and launches them when the time is right. His means of punishing the violent and removing corruption, thereby cleansing all within the Four Seas, depend on truly comprehending the root without busying himself with the branches, and discerning the essentials without being confused by particulars. People see that a true king has rules for regulating his troops, and some suppose that herein lies the means of bringing order to all under Heaven. They do not realize that these are not the fundamental essentials. A man of old said: “Rules arise from righteousness; righteousness arises from what suits the multitude; what suits the multitude accords with people’s hearts.” This captures it well. Tradition holds that the Six Secret Teachings (Liu Tao) was written by Taigong. Though I do not venture to believe this entirely, it records his telling King Wen: “When the great light emerges, all things are illuminated; when great righteousness is manifested, all things benefit; when the great army sets forth, all things submit.” Are these not truly sound words?
