title: 嘉靖四十年浙江武舉鄉試錄
text:
靈也衆陽之精昭明之大表光景之大紀也內
明玄黃五色變化以象人君精精似青翼翼似
黑玄玄似赤縞縞似白煌煌似黃光照無主不
可以一色名是謂大明固天下之至神也自其
出於暘谷浴於咸池拂於扶桑至於曲阿臨于
曾泉吞吐乎雲烟莽蒼之表而昭揭乎璇穹玉
宇之中則窮簷蔀屋之所幽閉陰山翳谷之所
蒙茸瑤池碧海之所杳靄跂行喙息之所奠麗
===
罔不洞然受燭毫毛無隱焉斯天下之至公也
王者繼天而起秉離明以照四方其德之併包
廣運也吾見其牢籠天地也磅礴陰陽也伸畏
四時也紀綱八極也其震耀宇宙也是太陽之
明也當夫海宇晏然泰階不攺群賢履職黎民
樂業天下和平人神休暢聖王拱揖穆清之上
而八紘四裔固皆納於光明而揚其和景矣皇
皇哉時也亦何以兵爲哉惟不幸而偶値世運
punctuated:
靈也，衆陽之精，昭明之大表，光景之大紀也。內明玄黃，五色變化，以象人君：精精似青，翼翼似黑，玄玄似赤，縞縞似白，煌煌似黃。光照無主，不可以一色名，是謂大明，固天下之至神也。自其出於暘谷，浴於咸池，拂於扶桑，至於曲阿，臨于曾泉，吞吐乎雲烟莽蒼之表，而昭揭乎璇穹玉宇之中，則窮簷蔀屋之所幽閉，陰山翳谷之所蒙茸，瑤池碧海之所杳靄，跂行喙息之所奠麗，罔不洞然受燭，毫毛無隱焉。斯天下之至公也。
王者繼天而起，秉離明以照四方。其德之併包廣運也，吾見其牢籠天地也，磅礴陰陽也，伸畏四時也，紀綱八極也，其震耀宇宙也，是太陽之明也。當夫海宇晏然，泰階不攺，群賢履職，黎民樂業，天下和平，人神休暢，聖王拱揖穆清之上，而八紘四裔固皆納於光明而揚其和景矣。皇皇哉，時也！亦何以兵爲哉？惟不幸而偶値世運
translation_en:
…a numinous radiance, the essence of all yang forces, the great emblem of brightness, and the great regulator of light. Within it shine the dark and yellow hues; its five colors change, providing an image of the ruler of men: brilliant, it resembles blue-green [?]; spreading like wings, it resembles black; deep and mysterious, it resembles red; gleaming like undyed silk, it resembles white; resplendent, it resembles yellow. No single hue predominates in its radiance, and it cannot be named by one color. This is called great illumination, surely the most numinous thing under Heaven. From its emergence at Yanggu, its bathing in Xianchi, and its brushing past Fusang, until it reaches Qu’a and looks down upon Zengquan, it issues from and enters clouds and mist beyond the dim expanses, shining aloft amid the jeweled vault of heaven. Thus the secluded darkness beneath humble eaves and thatched roofs, the dense growth on shaded mountains and in obscured valleys, the distant haze over Yaochi and the blue seas, and the places where creatures that crawl and breathe make their homes—all receive its penetrating illumination, with not so much as a hair left hidden. This is the utmost impartiality under Heaven.
The true king arises in succession to Heaven, wielding the brightness of Li, the trigram of fire, to illuminate the four quarters. In the all-embracing reach of his virtue, I see him encompass Heaven and Earth, permeate yin and yang, extend his majesty through the four seasons [?], order the eight extremities, and shine mightily throughout the universe. This is the brightness of the sun. When all within the seas is tranquil, the stars of the Celestial Stairway remain constant, worthy men fulfill their offices, and the common people delight in their livelihoods, all under Heaven enjoys peace and harmony, and humans and spirits alike are blessed and content. The sage king sits with hands folded in the pure serenity of his lofty court, while the eight expanses and the peoples of the four outer regions are all embraced within his light and spread its gentle radiance. How splendid an age! What need could there be for arms? Only if, unhappily, one should chance upon an age when the course of the world…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江武舉鄉試錄
text:
晦蒙氤氳閉塞暴雹恣行奸慝叢委譬諸羲和
頓轡薄於虞泉渝于豢谷是謂定昏斯陰翳鬱
盈而陽道或幾乎息矣乃聖人者乘運而興握
符而起紹百王之荒屯因造化之盪滌則不得
不假諸兵以掃除而開闢之於是有車甲之奉
有漆膠之材有旗鼓之司以待兵之用有蒐苗
之令有獮狩之役有訓習之法以時兵之教有
將佐之任有卒伍之班有營衛之制以肅兵之
===
紀有魚麗鵞鸛之陳有方圓牝牡之形有天地
風雲龍虎鳥蛇之名以盡兵之變有陰陽寒暑
之候有險易遠近廣狹之規有仁智勇信嚴之
德有曲制官道主用之術以神兵之機若是乎
其詳也然皆末也而非其本要也是故鉤戟長
鎩革車奄戶縵輪籠轂險道疾馳此可與致用
而非所恃以爲勝也十則圍之五則攻之倍則
分之敵則戰之此可與慮敵而非所恃以爲安
punctuated:
晦蒙氤氳，閉塞暴雹恣行，奸慝叢委。譬諸羲和頓轡，薄於虞泉，渝于豢谷，是謂定昏。斯陰翳鬱盈，而陽道或幾乎息矣。乃聖人者乘運而興，握符而起，紹百王之荒屯，因造化之盪滌，則不得不假諸兵以掃除而開闢之。
於是有車甲之奉，有漆膠之材，有旗鼓之司，以待兵之用；有蒐苗之令，有獮狩之役，有訓習之法，以時兵之教；有將佐之任，有卒伍之班，有營衛之制，以肅兵之紀；有魚麗鵞鸛之陳，有方圓牝牡之形，有天地風雲龍虎鳥蛇之名，以盡兵之變；有陰陽寒暑之候，有險易遠近廣狹之規，有仁智勇信嚴之德，有曲制官道主用之術，以神兵之機。若是乎其詳也！然皆末也，而非其本要也。
是故鉤戟長鎩，革車奄戶，縵輪籠轂，險道疾馳，此可與致用，而非所恃以爲勝也；十則圍之，五則攻之，倍則分之，敵則戰之，此可與慮敵，而非所恃以爲安
translation_en:
…darkness and murk gather, obstruction and violent hail run rampant, and wickedness accumulates. It is as though Xihe reined in the sun’s chariot, approaching Yuquan and passing into Huangu [?]: this is called settled darkness. Then gloomy shadows gather thickly, and the course of yang almost ceases. A sage therefore arises in response to the movement of destiny, bearing the token of his mandate. Inheriting the desolation and adversity left by successive kings, and following the cleansing action of creation, he cannot but employ arms to sweep away obstructions and open the world anew.
Thus there are provisions of chariots and armor, materials of lacquer and glue, and officers responsible for banners and drums, to make ready the equipment of war. There are orders for the spring and summer hunts, undertakings for the autumn and winter hunts, and methods of drill and practice, to conduct military instruction at the proper seasons. There are appointments of commanders and their assistants, arrangements of soldiers in units, and systems of encampment and guard duty, to enforce military discipline. There are the Fish-Scale, Goose, and Crane formations; square and circular, female and male configurations; and formations named Heaven, Earth, Wind, Cloud, Dragon, Tiger, Bird, and Snake, to encompass every military variation. There are observations of yin and yang, cold and heat; rules concerning difficult and easy terrain, distance, breadth, and narrowness; the virtues of benevolence, wisdom, courage, trustworthiness, and strictness; and techniques for organizing units, establishing officers’ responsibilities, and managing expenditure, to impart marvelous efficacy to military operations. How detailed all this is! Yet these are all peripheral matters, not the essential foundation.
Thus hooked halberds and long spears, leather-armored chariots with covered openings [?], covered wheels and encased hubs [?], and swift driving along dangerous roads may serve practical purposes, but they are not what one relies upon for victory. “With ten times the enemy’s strength, surround him; with five times his strength, attack him; with twice his strength, divide him; when evenly matched, fight him”: these may serve in calculating how to confront the enemy, but they are not what one relies upon for security…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江武舉鄉試錄
text:
也高丘弗向背丘弗逆佯北弗追銳卒弗攻歸
師弗遏圍師必闕此可與察機而非所恃以爲
威也因間者因其鄉內間者因其官反間者因
其敵死間者因其誑生間者因其報此可與多
誤而非所恃以爲成也嗟乎聖人亦何樂於以
兵爲哉易之師曰地中有水師君子以容民畜
衆夫師之爲義烈矣而顧以容民畜衆繫之此
推本聖人之心而言之也蓋王者天下之義主
===
而王者之兵以義而舉者也其動也極天下之
至神固大明之爲象也其舉也極天下之至公
即大明之普照也今夫爝火之燎于原燐火之
出于野其一時揚光吐焰非不灼然明也然發
之無本而施之有限秪見其不旋踵滅息矣斯
螢燭之末光爾安能對揚景鑠而儀炳靈曜哉
惟太陽一出而光徧海宇巍巍翼翼四海無不
仰其照也晃晃朗朗萬物無不被其華也舉天
punctuated:
也。高丘弗向，背丘弗逆，佯北弗追，銳卒弗攻，歸師弗遏，圍師必闕，此可與察機，而非所恃以爲威也。因間者，因其鄉；內間者，因其官；反間者，因其敵；死間者，因其誑；生間者，因其報。此可與多誤，而非所恃以爲成也。嗟乎！聖人亦何樂於以兵爲哉？《易》之《師》曰：「地中有水，師；君子以容民畜衆。」夫師之爲義烈矣，而顧以容民畜衆繫之，此推本聖人之心而言之也。蓋王者，天下之義主，而王者之兵，以義而舉者也。其動也，極天下之至神，固大明之爲象也；其舉也，極天下之至公，即大明之普照也。

今夫爝火之燎于原，燐火之出于野，其一時揚光吐焰，非不灼然明也。然發之無本，而施之有限，秪見其不旋踵滅息矣。斯螢燭之末光爾，安能對揚景鑠，而儀炳靈曜哉？惟太陽一出，而光徧海宇，巍巍翼翼，四海無不仰其照也；晃晃朗朗，萬物無不被其華也。舉天
translation_en:
…secure. Do not advance toward high ground; do not oppose an enemy with a hill at its back; do not pursue a feigned retreat; do not attack crack troops; do not obstruct an army returning home; and always leave an opening when surrounding an army. These precepts can help one discern opportunities, but cannot be relied upon to establish commanding might. Local spies draw on the enemy’s villagers; internal spies, on its officials; double agents, on the enemy; expendable spies, on deception; and surviving spies, on their reports. These can help multiply the enemy’s errors [?], but cannot be relied upon to secure success. Alas! What pleasure could the sage take in employing arms? The Army hexagram of the Book of Changes says: “Within the earth there is water: the Army. The gentleman accordingly accommodates the people and nurtures the multitude.” The meaning of “army” is fierce indeed, yet accommodating the people and nurturing the multitude are attached to it. This speaks by tracing the matter back to the sage’s underlying intentions. For the true king is the lord of righteousness for all under Heaven, and the true king’s forces are raised in righteousness. Their movements exemplify the utmost spiritual efficacy under Heaven, taking the sun as their image; their mobilization exemplifies the utmost impartiality under Heaven, like the sun’s universal illumination.

Now, torch fires blazing on the plain and ghostly fires appearing in the wild do, for a time, cast light and pour forth flames: they certainly shine brightly. Yet their arising has no enduring foundation, and their reach is limited; before one can turn on one’s heel, they are extinguished. These are merely the faint gleams of fireflies and candles. How could they match that magnificent radiance and emulate the brilliance of the divine luminary? Only when the sun rises does its light spread throughout the realm. Lofty and majestic, it leaves none within the Four Seas who do not look up to its illumination; dazzling and luminous, it leaves none among the myriad things untouched by its splendor. Of all things under Heaven…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江武舉鄉試錄
text:
下之至明莫有踰此者而王者之兵憫濁世而
發憤散皇明以燭幽固本天下之大義也其初
舉兵也告于皇天上帝日月星辰祠于后土四
海神祇乃徵師於諸侯曰某爲不道征之以兵
百官布令於軍曰入罪人之地無爲暴虐是以
天下之目視也以天下之耳聽也以天下之智
慮也以天下之力爭也而王者之心不將不迎
應而不藏坦然與天下共之而無欝其章灼昭
著如大明之中天焉斯謂天下之大兵也由是
桴鼓所向烏舉飆發天下莫不響震景從士女
迎於郊筐篚陳於道市肆安於國謳歌載於途
蒸爲太和釀爲元化而向之雰埃霾霧咸散於
飄風銷於朗爛矣嗟乎激水無形其至於漂石
者勢也彍弩無足其至於百步者機也大兵不
智不力而横騖天下莫有敵者義也此夫不衝
機而攻也無溝塹而守也微乎微乎入於無形
punctuated:
下之至明，莫有踰此者。而王者之兵，憫濁世而發憤，散皇明以燭幽，固本天下之大義也。其初舉兵也，告于皇天上帝、日月星辰，祠于后土、四海神祇，乃徵師於諸侯，曰：「某爲不道，征之以兵。」百官布令於軍，曰：「入罪人之地，無爲暴虐。」是以天下之目視也，以天下之耳聽也，以天下之智慮也，以天下之力爭也。而王者之心，不將不迎，應而不藏，坦然與天下共之而無欝。其章灼昭著，如大明之中天焉。斯謂天下之大兵也。由是桴鼓所向，烏舉飆發，天下莫不響震景從。士女迎於郊，筐篚陳於道，市肆安於國，謳歌載於途。蒸爲太和，釀爲元化，而向之雰埃霾霧，咸散於飄風，銷於朗爛矣。
嗟乎！激水無形，其至於漂石者，勢也；彍弩無足，其至於百步者，機也；大兵不智不力，而横騖天下莫有敵者，義也。此夫不衝機而攻也，無溝塹而守也。微乎！微乎！入於無形。
translation_en:
…of all the brightest things under Heaven, none surpasses this. The army of a true king, moved by compassion for a corrupt age, rises in indignation and spreads august radiance to illuminate the darkness: it is firmly rooted in the great righteousness of all under Heaven. When the king first raises his army, he announces this to August Heaven, the Supreme Lord, the sun, moon, and stars, and offers sacrifices to Sovereign Earth and the spirits of the Four Seas. He then summons troops from the feudal lords, saying: “So-and-so has acted contrary to the Way; chastise him by force of arms.” The officials proclaim orders to the army: “When entering the offender’s territory, commit no violence or cruelty.” Thus he sees through the eyes of all under Heaven, hears through their ears, deliberates with their wisdom, and contends with their strength. Yet the king’s mind neither clings to what departs nor anticipates what comes; it responds without storing things up. Openly, he shares it with all under Heaven, keeping nothing pent up. Its manifest brilliance is like the sun at the zenith. This is what is called the great army of all under Heaven. Wherever its drumbeats lead, it rises like crows [?] and advances like a whirlwind; everyone under Heaven responds like an echo and follows like a shadow. Men and women welcome it in the outskirts; baskets of offerings are set out along the roads; shops remain secure within the realm; songs of praise fill the highways. This influence suffuses the world with supreme harmony and brings about fundamental transformation. The dust, haze, and murk of former days are all dispersed by the rushing wind and dissolved in the radiance.
Alas! Surging water has no fixed shape; that it can carry away stones is due to its momentum. A drawn crossbow has no feet; that its shot reaches a hundred paces is due to its mechanism. The great army does not rely on cleverness or force; that it ranges across all under Heaven without an equal is due to righteousness. This is attacking without siege engines [?] and defending without ditches or moats. Subtle indeed! Subtle indeed! It enters the realm of the formless…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江武舉鄉試錄
text:
淵乎淵乎達於無聲非夫天下之神武上聖之
皇德疇能之哉司馬法曰古者以仁爲本以義
治之之謂正太史公亦曰形勢雖强要以仁義
爲本言聖王之大兵誠在此而不在彼也至孫
吳者流著爲兵法以求得志於天下廢王者之
務而事狙獪之術捐道德之敎而詳法制之用
詭大道而任小數雖或攻勝戰取世皆以知兵
歸之然爝火而已爾燐火而已爾一遇太陽則
===
奄然銷歇矣欲以繼明於天下何得哉故有戰
至於焚雍門而天下不以爲兢勞至於絶地脉
而天下不以爲功威至於封狼望之野絶葱嶺
之塵而天下不以爲武謂其所恃者末也乃若
聖王之兵一發則駕御六合檢制四海而天下
莫不心服蓋其神哉非萬物所能踰也然以義
動以時發聖人無所庸心於其間也嗟乎以兵
服天下豈直非聖人之心哉蓋尤有大不得已
punctuated: 淵乎淵乎，達於無聲！非夫天下之神武、上聖之皇德，疇能之哉？《司馬法》曰：「古者以仁爲本，以義治之，之謂正。」太史公亦曰：「形勢雖强，要以仁義爲本。」言聖王之大兵誠在此而不在彼也。至孫吳者流，著爲兵法，以求得志於天下，廢王者之務而事狙獪之術，捐道德之敎而詳法制之用，詭大道而任小數。雖或攻勝戰取，世皆以知兵歸之，然爝火而已爾，燐火而已爾，一遇太陽，則奄然銷歇矣。欲以繼明於天下，何得哉？故有戰至於焚雍門，而天下不以爲兢；勞至於絶地脉，而天下不以爲功；威至於封狼望之野、絶葱嶺之塵，而天下不以爲武，謂其所恃者末也。乃若聖王之兵，一發則駕御六合，檢制四海，而天下莫不心服。蓋其神哉，非萬物所能踰也。然以義動，以時發，聖人無所庸心於其間也。嗟乎！以兵服天下，豈直非聖人之心哉？蓋尤有大不得已
translation_en:
…How unfathomable, how unfathomable—reaching the realm of soundlessness! Who could accomplish this without the spirit-like martial prowess of all under Heaven and the august virtue of the highest sage? The Methods of the Minister of War (Sima fa) says: “In antiquity, they took benevolence as the foundation and governed through righteousness; this was called uprightness.” The Grand Astrologer likewise said: “Though strategic circumstances are advantageous, the essential thing is to take benevolence and righteousness as the foundation.” These words mean that the great military power of a sage king truly rests in these things, rather than those other things.

As for men of the school of Sun and Wu, they wrote military treatises to achieve their ambitions in the world. They abandoned the proper concerns of a true king and practiced cunning tricks; they discarded the teachings of the Way and virtue and elaborated the application of laws and institutions. They departed from the Great Way and relied on petty stratagems. Although they sometimes prevailed in attacks and won gains in battle, and everyone credited them with understanding warfare, theirs was merely the light of a torch, merely a ghostly phosphorescence. Once it encounters the sun, it abruptly fades away. How could they hope to provide enduring light to all under Heaven?

Thus some fought so far as to burn the Yong Gate, yet the world did not regard this as an achievement [?]; some exerted themselves to the point of severing the veins of the earth, yet the world did not regard this as meritorious. Some extended their might so far as to raise a sacrificial mound in the wilds of Langwang [?] and put an end to the dust of warfare at the Congling Mountains, yet the world did not regard this as martial prowess. This is because what they relied upon was merely peripheral.

With the armies of a sage king, however, a single deployment brings the six directions under command and the lands within the Four Seas under control, and everyone in the world submits wholeheartedly. Such spirit-like efficacy cannot be surpassed by any being. Yet the sage acts in accordance with righteousness and deploys at the proper time, without having to exert his mind in the process. Alas! To subdue the world by force of arms is surely more than merely contrary to the sage’s wishes: there must, moreover, be some compelling necessity…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江武舉鄉試錄
text:
者矣夫陽春煦物大明當天萬物之被照者舉
欣欣向之有怡愉融液之色至於秋陽則就暵
者思避焉以爲熯烈之威不若春陽之爲和也
然則兵也其秋之陽乎與其爲赫怒以安天下
寧爲兩階之干羽與其爲大介以定天下寧爲
九官之揖遜故曰兵者聖人不得已而用之也
雖然文武並用長久之術也聖王安不忘危治
不忘亂故雖不佳兵而實未嘗忘武事以武有
===
時而用也今夫太陽一也當春則煦遇秋則烈
化之所以爲神也而萬物之被其照則一也然
則聖王御極豈能忘武哉若薦紳之徒居平世
而諱談兵者吾不知其可也
又
周曰廉
馬上中七箭
步下中三箭
punctuated:
者矣。夫陽春煦物，大明當天，萬物之被照者舉欣欣向之，有怡愉融液之色。至於秋陽，則就暵者思避焉，以爲熯烈之威不若春陽之爲和也。然則兵也，其秋之陽乎？與其爲赫怒以安天下，寧爲兩階之干羽；與其爲大介以定天下，寧爲九官之揖遜。故曰：「兵者，聖人不得已而用之也。」雖然，文武並用，長久之術也。聖王安不忘危，治不忘亂，故雖不佳兵，而實未嘗忘武事，以武有時而用也。今夫太陽一也，當春則煦，遇秋則烈，化之所以爲神也；而萬物之被其照則一也。然則聖王御極，豈能忘武哉？若薦紳之徒居平世而諱談兵者，吾不知其可也。

又。
周曰廉，馬上中七箭，步下中三箭。
translation_en:
…there are indeed circumstances in which it is utterly unavoidable. When the spring sunshine warms all things and the great luminary stands in the sky, everything upon which it shines turns joyfully toward it, displaying an air of contentment and harmony. Under the autumn sun, however, those exposed to its scorching heat seek shelter, considering its fierce intensity inferior to the gentleness of the spring sun. Is warfare, then, like the autumn sun? Rather than unleash thunderous anger to bring peace to All-under-Heaven, better to perform the dance with shields and feathers between the two stairways; rather than don full armor to settle All-under-Heaven, better to practice the bowing and yielding of the nine officers. Thus it is said: “Arms are something the sage employs only when he has no alternative.”

Nevertheless, employing both civil and military means is the way to endure. In peace, the sage king does not forget danger; amid order, he does not forget disorder. Thus, although he does not delight in arms, he has never forgotten military affairs, for there are times when military force must be used. Now, the sun is one and the same: in spring it warms, while in autumn it scorches. This is what makes its transforming power wondrous; yet its illumination of all things remains the same. How, then, could a sage king occupying the throne forget military matters? As for those members of the official class who live in peaceful times and shun discussion of warfare, I cannot see how their position is defensible.

Another composition.
Zhou Yuelian scored seven arrow hits on horseback and three on foot.

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江武舉鄉試錄
text:
聖人無所利于天下而天下之望治者不能自
外于聖人聖人之有事也亦因乎時焉而無所
容心其間也夫聖人曷嘗以有心應天下之故
哉天下之故至變而聖人之心至虛天未定也
不能必其来勢已積也不能諉之去有心以應
之則私焉耳已矧當征伐際革命林林而引領
望治者殆盡天下廼大故孰稱是焉而聖人顧
以有心臨之則利天下者之爲也利天下者將
===
不爲天下所利顧天下人心翕然向之而莫或
忤也理哉是故大義發於聖人聖人無心也而
萬物利之非聖人之所與知也大兵舉于聖人
聖人無心也而萬物服之亦非聖人之所與知
也殆象諸天乎大明一發而萬物皆照天無心
於明而物自忘其照然則知天道之神不謂照
物而發其明則知聖人之德不爲利天下而有
事乎義且兵矣我聞之古語上世有天下者栢
punctuated: 聖人無所利于天下，而天下之望治者不能自外于聖人。聖人之有事也，亦因乎時焉，而無所容心其間也。夫聖人曷嘗以有心應天下之故哉？天下之故至變，而聖人之心至虛。天未定也，不能必其来；勢已積也，不能諉之去。有心以應之，則私焉耳已。矧當征伐、際革命，林林而引領望治者殆盡天下，廼大故孰稱是焉？而聖人顧以有心臨之，則利天下者之爲也。利天下者將不爲天下所利，顧天下人心翕然向之而莫或忤也，理哉？是故大義發於聖人，聖人無心也，而萬物利之，非聖人之所與知也。大兵舉于聖人，聖人無心也，而萬物服之，亦非聖人之所與知也。殆象諸天乎？大明一發，而萬物皆照。天無心於明，而物自忘其照。然則知天道之神，不謂照物而發其明，則知聖人之德，不爲利天下而有事乎義且兵矣。我聞之古語，上世有天下者，栢
translation_en:
The sage seeks no gain from All-under-Heaven, yet those throughout the realm who hope for good government cannot stand apart from him. When the sage takes action, he responds to the times, allowing no deliberate personal intention to intervene. When has the sage ever responded to the affairs of All-under-Heaven with such intention? Those affairs are infinitely changeable, while the sage’s mind is utterly empty. Before Heaven’s course is settled, its coming cannot be assured; once circumstances have gathered force, they cannot be dismissed. To respond with deliberate intention would merely be selfishness. How much more so amid punitive campaigns and a change of the mandate, when the multitudes craning their necks in hope of good government comprise almost everyone under Heaven! What great crisis could compare with this? Yet if the sage confronted it with deliberate personal intention, he would be acting as one who sought to profit from All-under-Heaven. One who seeks such profit will receive no benefit from All-under-Heaven. Could it then be reasonable for the hearts of all its people to turn unanimously toward him, with none opposing him?

Thus, when great righteousness issues from the sage, he has no deliberate intention; that the myriad beings benefit from it is not something he concerns himself with. When the sage raises a great army, he has no deliberate intention; that the myriad beings submit to it is likewise not something he concerns himself with. Does he not, perhaps, resemble Heaven? Once its great light shines forth, the myriad beings are all illuminated. Heaven has no deliberate intention of shining, and beings themselves remain oblivious to its illumination. Thus, if one understands the wondrous working of Heaven’s Way—that it does not emit its light with the purpose of illuminating things—one understands that the sage’s virtue does not undertake acts of righteousness and warfare for the sake of gaining from All-under-Heaven. I have heard it in an ancient saying: among those who possessed All-under-Heaven in remote antiquity, Bai…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江武舉鄉試錄
text:
皇栗陸以前爲而不有應而不求執大象也鴻
蒿世及以一民也汾穆之風渾噩之治郁郁嶷
嶷上下安之天下不知所謂兵也天下不知所
謂兵而聖人者顧樂乎觀兵於天下豈其心之
得已哉夫聖人非不欲終天地而汾穆渾噩焉
以竟游衍于太荒之始也亦非不欲盡民物而
休息安養焉以共樂利于熈皞之化也而不能
盡如其意者時適爲之是故任智自神橫于共
===
工好兵喜亂作于蚩尤于是乎祝融之師阪泉
之戰不可已也然則自有生民茲殆天道之一
小變乎而榆罔軒皇固已漸頹于太昊之世矣
夫固時爲之也嗣是九黎拂亂天下惑恠暨摯
荒滛諸侯廢之然承祧于高陽翼善于陶唐梗
化者傾心靡風者於變可以德感可以誠動可
以聲教行而政令敷之二聖人固無樂乎其事
於兵也又嗣是而投凶而格苗以象刑以舞羽
punctuated: 皇、栗陸以前，爲而不有，應而不求，執大象也。鴻蒿世及，以一民也。汾穆之風，渾噩之治，郁郁嶷嶷，上下安之，天下不知所謂兵也。天下不知所謂兵，而聖人者顧樂乎觀兵於天下，豈其心之得已哉？夫聖人非不欲終天地而汾穆渾噩焉，以竟游衍于太荒之始也；亦非不欲盡民物而休息安養焉，以共樂利于熈皞之化也。而不能盡如其意者，時適爲之。是故任智自神，橫于共工；好兵喜亂，作于蚩尤。于是乎祝融之師、阪泉之戰，不可已也。然則自有生民，茲殆天道之一小變乎？而榆罔、軒皇固已漸頹于太昊之世矣。夫固時爲之也。嗣是，九黎拂亂，天下惑恠，暨摯荒滛，諸侯廢之。然承祧于高陽，翼善于陶唐，梗化者傾心，靡風者於變，可以德感，可以誠動，可以聲教行而政令敷之。二聖人固無樂乎其事於兵也。又嗣是而投凶而格苗，以象刑，以舞羽。
translation_en:
…[Bai]huang and Lilu and those before them acted without possessing, responded without seeking, and held fast to the Great Image. In the primordial age [?], successive rulers kept the people united. With an atmosphere of harmony and reverence [?] and government of unspoiled simplicity, flourishing and lofty, those above and below rested content. The world did not know what warfare meant. If the world did not know warfare, could the sages nevertheless have delighted in displaying their armies before it? Could this have been something their hearts freely chose?

The sages certainly wished to preserve this harmony and pristine simplicity [?] for as long as Heaven and Earth endured, roaming forever in the primordial age. They also wished to give all people and creatures rest, peace, and nourishment, so that all might share the happiness and benefits of a radiant, harmonious civilizing influence. That they could not fully realize their wishes was due to the circumstances of their times. Thus reliance on cunning and pretensions to divine power ran rampant in Gonggong, while delight in warfare and disorder arose in Chiyou. Consequently, Zhurong’s campaign and the battle of Banquan became unavoidable. Was this perhaps a small change in the Way of Heaven since the birth of humankind? Yet under Yuwang and the Yellow Emperor, decline from the age of Taihao had already gradually begun. It was indeed the times that brought this about.

Thereafter, the Jiuli brought disorder, and the world fell into confusion and aberration. When Zhi became dissolute, the regional lords deposed him. Yet with Gaoyang succeeding to the ancestral succession and Taotang fostering goodness, those who resisted moral transformation gave their allegiance, and those who yielded to their influence were transformed. Virtue could move them, sincerity could stir them, and moral instruction could spread while governmental commands were promulgated. These two sages certainly took no pleasure in resorting to arms. Thereafter came the banishment of the wicked and the winning over of the Miao, through symbolic punishments and dances with feathers…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江武舉鄉試錄
text:
無所事武則協帝之德亦所值幸焉至于桀之
不道乃暴戾頑狠天下顫然而鳴條之師三朡
之逐南巢之放勢于是乎不可已也嗚呼湯之
不幸也非得已也知湯不得已之心則可以求
文王之心而推大明照物之論矣天下之生久
矣一治一亂湯之時天道之一大變乎而文王
者又值其變矣夫有商罪浮于桀剥喪元良毒
痡四海崇信奸回以師保放黜矣典刑屏棄矣
===
謂巳有天命謂敬不足行謂祭無益謂暴無傷
斮朝涉之脛剖賢人之心奇技淫巧婦人是悅
而臣下化之脅權相滅草竊姦宄師師非度當
是時天下之民苦塗炭急水火天地爲之昏墊
日月爲之晦冥蓋造化巳厭而思治者饑渴矣
文王誠何忍恝然於是也夫文王不忍於民也
尤不忍于殷也羑里之囚譖于崇侯文王甘之
不以爲懟洛西之獻請除炮烙文王爲之不以
punctuated: 無所事武，則協帝之德，亦所值幸焉。至于桀之不道，乃暴戾頑狠，天下顫然，而鳴條之師、三朡之逐、南巢之放，勢于是乎不可已也。嗚呼！湯之不幸也，非得已也。知湯不得已之心，則可以求文王之心，而推大明照物之論矣。天下之生久矣，一治一亂，湯之時，天道之一大變乎！而文王者，又值其變矣。夫有商罪浮于桀，剥喪元良，毒痡四海，崇信奸回，以師保放黜矣，典刑屏棄矣。謂巳有天命，謂敬不足行，謂祭無益，謂暴無傷。斮朝涉之脛，剖賢人之心，奇技淫巧，婦人是悅。而臣下化之，脅權相滅，草竊姦宄，師師非度。當是時，天下之民苦塗炭，急水火，天地爲之昏墊，日月爲之晦冥。蓋造化巳厭，而思治者饑渴矣。文王誠何忍恝然於是也？夫文王不忍於民也，尤不忍于殷也。羑里之囚，譖于崇侯，文王甘之，不以爲懟；洛西之獻，請除炮烙，文王爲之，不以
translation_en:
…There was no occasion to employ military force; thus, for the one whose virtue accorded with the emperor’s, the circumstances he encountered were also fortunate. But when Jie departed from the Way and became violent, cruel, obstinate, and ruthless, all under Heaven trembled. The campaign at Mingtiao, the pursuit to Sanzong, and the banishment to Nanchao became unavoidable under these circumstances. Alas! Tang’s misfortune was that he had no choice. If we understand the heart of Tang, who could not do otherwise, we can seek to understand King Wen’s heart and develop the argument concerning great brightness illuminating all things.

Human life under Heaven has endured for a long time, with order and disorder succeeding one another. Was not Tang’s age a great turning in the Way of Heaven? King Wen, too, encountered such a turning. The ruler of Shang committed crimes exceeding Jie’s: he destroyed the foremost worthy men, afflicted all within the Four Seas, and honored and trusted the wicked and perverse. The Grand Preceptor and Grand Guardian were banished and dismissed [?], and established laws were cast aside. He claimed that he possessed Heaven’s mandate, that reverence was not worth practicing, that sacrifices were of no benefit, and that violence could do no harm. He cut through the shins of those who crossed a stream in the morning and cut open a worthy man’s heart. With outlandish skills and extravagant craftsmanship, he sought only to please a woman. His ministers followed his example, wielding power coercively to destroy one another, committing theft and treachery, and imitating one another in defying established standards.

At that time, the people under Heaven suffered as though mired in mud and burning charcoal, their distress as urgent as if they were trapped in flood and fire. Heaven and earth were plunged into darkness and ruin, and the sun and moon grew dim. Indeed, the powers of creation had already grown weary of this, and those who yearned for order hungered and thirsted for it. How could King Wen bear to remain indifferent to this? King Wen could not bear the people’s suffering, and still less could he bear the plight of Yin. Imprisoned at Youli through the slander of the Marquis of Chong, King Wen accepted his lot without resentment. He offered the lands west of the Luo River and requested the abolition of the burning-pillar torture; King Wen did this without regarding it as…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江武舉鄉試錄
text:
爲諂此何心哉兾其或少悟而改圖焉可以逺
暴而爲仁也至于賜弓矢鈇鉞有兵權專征伐
三分有二諸侯歸之則弔伐之舉易巳然一怒
整旅聞遏密閭降崇又聞戡黎矣移師而受乃
振槁然不遺力也顧以服事之文王又爲之不
以爲瀆此又何心哉兾其或少悟而改圖焉可
以逺暴而爲仁也是心也孔子得之故云至德
孟子亦得之而度其所值乃曰賢人輔相之久
===
則難變也然則紂一變而更化焉即罔欲弗喪
民心可回也茲固文王之爲心也而卒至于錮
惡不悛莫可解焉則天下之勢巳積而文王之
爲心不復可爲望是故商王虐極助予憂民之
問一召太公而詢之嗚呼此其心固大有所不
得巳也公爲之言曰大明一發萬物皆照文王
之爲心公固契之深矣夫晝夜相推日月之明
生焉天之道何心於明也天惟無心於明乃其
punctuated:
爲諂。此何心哉？兾其或少悟而改圖焉，可以逺暴而爲仁也。至于賜弓矢鈇鉞，有兵權，專征伐，三分有二，諸侯歸之，則弔伐之舉易巳。然一怒整旅，聞遏密閭，降崇，又聞戡黎矣。移師而受乃振槁，然不遺力也。顧以服事之，文王又爲之，不以爲瀆。此又何心哉？兾其或少悟而改圖焉，可以逺暴而爲仁也。是心也，孔子得之，故云至德；孟子亦得之，而度其所值，乃曰：「賢人輔相之久，則難變也。」然則紂一變而更化焉，即罔欲弗喪，民心可回也。茲固文王之爲心也。而卒至于錮惡不悛，莫可解焉，則天下之勢巳積，而文王之爲心不復可爲望。是故「商王虐極，助予憂民」之問，一召太公而詢之。嗚呼！此其心固大有所不得巳也。公爲之言曰：「大明一發，萬物皆照。」文王之爲心，公固契之深矣。

夫晝夜相推，日月之明生焉，天之道何心於明也？天惟無心於明，乃其
translation_en:
…regard it as flattery. What intention lay behind this? He hoped that the king might awaken somewhat and change his course, abandoning cruelty and practicing benevolence. When King Wen was granted bows and arrows and execution axes, holding military authority and independently conducting punitive campaigns, possessing two-thirds of the realm and receiving the allegiance of the regional lords, it would have been easy for him to launch a campaign to relieve the suffering people and punish their oppressor. Once roused to anger, he marshaled his troops; we hear of his checking Mi [?] and subduing Chong, and also of his conquering Li. Had he turned his army against Shou, it would have been like shaking down withered wood [?]; nevertheless, he spared no effort. Yet King Wen continued to serve him, without regarding this as a debasement. What intention, again, lay behind this? He hoped that the king might awaken somewhat and change his course, abandoning cruelty and practicing benevolence. Confucius understood this intention and therefore called his virtue supreme. Mencius also understood it; assessing the circumstances King Wen encountered, he said: “When worthy men have long assisted a ruler, change is difficult.” Thus, if Zhou had changed and reformed his government—even though ‘none who pursue desire escape ruin’ [?]—the people's allegiance could have been recovered. Such indeed was King Wen's intention. But in the end Zhou became entrenched in evil and remained unrepentant, beyond all remedy. The forces shaping the realm had already gathered momentum, and King Wen could no longer hope to realize his intention. Hence he summoned Taigong and put this question to him: “The king of Shang's cruelty has reached its utmost extreme. Help me in my concern for the people.” Alas! His heart was truly compelled by circumstances beyond his control. Taigong told him: “Once the great light shines forth, all things are illuminated.” Taigong indeed understood King Wen's intention profoundly.

Day and night succeed one another, and the light of the sun and moon arises from this. What deliberate intention to illuminate does the Way of Heaven possess? It is precisely because Heaven has no deliberate intention to illuminate that its…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江武舉鄉試錄
text:
照普治亂相沿弔伐之兵舉焉聖人之心亦何
心於兵也聖人惟無心於兵乃其仁普惟其時
焉耳已時所至明生于日月天不能違也兵舉
於弔伐聖人不能違也而實非其心也是故太
公言之文王之爲心益有所不得已也事殷之
禮終其身不變焉而會孟津次河朔誓牧野仗
黄鉞秉白旄稱干比戈恭行天罰至武王而後
舉之彼其心尚復有厚望於當時也而時之及
===
勢之積也天與之人歸之遵養時晦之餘在武
王有不能却其来而使去諸已者固天爲之也
是故邦甸侯衛奔走豆籩者會于未期单食壺
漿篚厥玄黄者来于不約血流漂杵倒戈後攻
者欵于不戰何爲其然也惡之集于紂也盈而
德之造于周也久武適其時也而非以富天下
也故其言曰祗承上帝以遏亂畧又曰百姓有
過在予一人此其心固文王所謂助予憂民之
punctuated: 照普。治亂相沿，弔伐之兵舉焉，聖人之心亦何心於兵也？聖人惟無心於兵，乃其仁普，惟其時焉耳已。時所至，明生于日月，天不能違也；兵舉於弔伐，聖人不能違也，而實非其心也。是故太公言之，文王之爲心益有所不得已也。事殷之禮，終其身不變焉；而會孟津，次河朔，誓牧野，仗黄鉞，秉白旄，稱干比戈，恭行天罰，至武王而後舉之。彼其心尚復有厚望於當時也，而時之及、勢之積也，天與之，人歸之，遵養時晦之餘，在武王有不能却其来而使去諸已者，固天爲之也。是故邦甸侯衛，奔走豆籩者，會于未期；单食壺漿，篚厥玄黄者，来于不約；血流漂杵，倒戈後攻者，欵于不戰。何爲其然也？惡之集于紂也盈，而德之造于周也久。武適其時也，而非以富天下也。故其言曰：「祗承上帝，以遏亂畧。」又曰：「百姓有過，在予一人。」此其心固文王所謂助予憂民之
translation_en:
…its illumination reaches everywhere. As order and disorder succeed one another, armies arise to succor the afflicted and punish the guilty. Yet what desire for warfare does the sage harbor in his heart? Precisely because the sage has no desire for warfare, his benevolence reaches everywhere. It is simply a matter of the time. When the time arrives, light issues from the sun and moon, and Heaven cannot act otherwise; armies arise to succor the afflicted and punish the guilty, and the sage cannot act otherwise. Yet warfare is not what he desires. Thus, when Taigong spoke these words, King Wen felt still more strongly that circumstances left him no choice. Throughout his life he never altered the rites by which he served the Yin dynasty. As for assembling at Mengjin, encamping north of the Yellow River, delivering the oath at Muye, wielding the yellow battle-axe, grasping the white yak-tail standard, raising shields and arraying dagger-axes, and reverently executing Heaven’s punishment—these actions were undertaken only in King Wu’s time. King Wen still cherished great hopes for his own age. But when the time arrived and circumstances had gathered force, Heaven bestowed its favor and the people turned their allegiance to Zhou. After the period of nurturing virtue while remaining in obscurity, King Wu could neither reject what came to him nor turn it away from himself. This was indeed Heaven’s doing.

Thus, those from the domains of the states, the royal lands, the lords, and the outer guards, who hurried to present ritual vessels of wood and bamboo, assembled before a date had been set. Those bringing baskets of food [?], pitchers of drink, and baskets filled with dark and yellow silks arrived without prior arrangement. Amid blood flowing deep enough to float pestles, those who reversed their weapons and attacked their own rear submitted without a fight. Why was this so? The evil accumulated by Zhòu, the Shang king, had reached its fullness, while the virtue cultivated by Zhou had developed over a long time. King Wu merely encountered the fitting moment; he did not act to enrich himself with possession of all under Heaven. Hence he said: “Reverently obeying the Lord on High, I restrain disorder and aggression.” He also said: “If the common people commit a fault, the responsibility rests with me alone.” This intention was indeed what King Wen meant by “help me care for the people”—the heart that…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江武舉鄉試錄
text:
心也抑不特爲文王之心固亦堯舜之爲心也
昔堯欲伐宗膾胥敖南面而不釋然以問之舜
舜曰三子者猶存乎蓬艾之間若不釋然何哉
昔者十日並出萬物皆照而況德之進乎日者
乎夫堯不釋然於三國之伐而舜則推置夫蓬
艾之情彼文武之爲心固堯舜之爲心也太公
照物之論固有所宗也已而或者乃曰武王非
聖人也孔子以大哉稱堯無爲道舜無間語禹
===
得仁予夷齊若罪武也然則謂湯武革命順乎
天而應乎人者何說耶殷之厭於天人極矣而
天休震動用附大邑適天人自然之合武王無
心之感其謂非聖也則當其時謂一德一心立
定厥功惟克永世者其曷捷影響之速而罔或
爽也又謂矢于牧野維予侯興上帝臨汝無貳
爾心者其又曷協衆願之同而無或携也是故
兵凶戰危聖人所懼好攻樂殺君子所罪有湯
punctuated: 心也。抑不特爲文王之心，固亦堯舜之爲心也。昔堯欲伐宗、膾、胥敖，南面而不釋然，以問之舜。舜曰：「三子者猶存乎蓬艾之間，若不釋然何哉？昔者十日並出，萬物皆照，而況德之進乎日者乎？」夫堯不釋然於三國之伐，而舜則推置夫蓬艾之情。彼文武之爲心，固堯舜之爲心也。太公照物之論，固有所宗也已。而或者乃曰：「武王非聖人也。孔子以『大哉』稱堯，『無爲』道舜，『無間』語禹，『得仁』予夷齊，若罪武也。」然則謂「湯武革命，順乎天而應乎人」者，何說耶？殷之厭於天人極矣，而天休震動，用附大邑，適天人自然之合，武王無心之感。其謂非聖也，則當其時謂「一德一心，立定厥功，惟克永世」者，其曷捷影響之速，而罔或爽也？又謂「矢于牧野，維予侯興。上帝臨汝，無貳爾心」者，其又曷協衆願之同，而無或携也？是故兵凶戰危，聖人所懼；好攻樂殺，君子所罪。有湯
translation_en:
…heart. Yet this was not merely King Wen’s heart; it was also the heart of Yao and Shun. Once Yao wished to attack Zong, Kuai, and Xu’ao, but as he sat facing south upon his throne, he felt uneasy and asked Shun about it. Shun said: “The rulers of those three states still dwell among the wild grasses. Why should you feel uneasy? Long ago, ten suns rose together and illuminated all things. How much more, then, can virtue that surpasses the sun!” Yao felt uneasy about attacking the three states, while Shun gave consideration to the circumstances of those living among the wild grasses. The hearts of Kings Wen and Wu were indeed the hearts of Yao and Shun. The Grand Duke’s argument about illuminating all things thus certainly had a source.

Yet some say: “King Wu was no sage. Confucius praised Yao as ‘great indeed,’ described Shun as governing ‘without action,’ said that Yu was ‘beyond reproach,’ and credited Boyi and Shuqi with ‘attaining benevolence,’ seemingly condemning King Wu.” How, then, are we to understand the statement that “Tang and Wu changed the mandate, following Heaven and responding to the people”? Heaven’s and the people’s rejection of Yin had reached its utmost limit. Heaven’s favor stirred into action, bringing allegiance to the great city: this was precisely the spontaneous accord of Heaven and the people, and the response elicited by King Wu without deliberate intent. If he was no sage, then why did the declaration of that time—“United in virtue and purpose, establish their achievement, that it may endure forever”—find fulfillment as swiftly as shadow follows form or echo follows sound, without any discrepancy? And why did the words “He swore an oath at Muye: ‘It is I who shall rise. The Lord on High watches over you; let your hearts not waver’” accord with the shared wishes of the multitude, without anyone falling away?

Thus, arms are inauspicious and warfare perilous: the sage fears them. A fondness for aggression and delight in killing are what the gentleman condemns. If one possesses the heart of Tang…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江武舉鄉試錄
text:
武之心則誅殘拯溺不失爲日月之明無是心
也而肆諸窮黷之智則以亂易亂亦何愈於桀
紂之暴矣是故伐原示信大蒐示禮謂少長可
用也乃施諸與塊觀裸之譬而不擒二毛不皷
不列者顧安於饗人用社之慘或者乃謂文王
之戰不是過哉是何異盜跖之分均出後稱仁
義也又繼此而椎爭七國民日糜爛遠搏四荒
國日虛耗嗚呼秦漢去三代未遠而先王訓典
===
文告之風固巳遐邈不復可追矣然則兵可盡
廢乎夫生之不傷者仁人之爲心也用之不暴
者王者之爲兵也故曰善爲國者不師善師者
不陣善陣者不戰達于此可以語序成之化矣
又
張　勲
馬上中八箭
步下中四箭
punctuated:
武之心，則誅殘拯溺，不失爲日月之明。無是心也，而肆諸窮黷之智，則以亂易亂，亦何愈於桀紂之暴矣？是故伐原示信，大蒐示禮，謂少長可用也，乃施諸與塊觀裸之譬；而不擒二毛、不皷不列者，顧安於饗人用社之慘。或者乃謂文王之戰不是過哉！是何異盜跖之分均出後稱仁義也？又繼此而椎爭七國，民日糜爛；遠搏四荒，國日虛耗。嗚呼！秦漢去三代未遠，而先王訓典文告之風，固巳遐邈，不復可追矣。然則兵可盡廢乎？夫生之不傷者，仁人之爲心也；用之不暴者，王者之爲兵也。故曰：「善爲國者不師，善師者不陣，善陣者不戰。」達于此，可以語序成之化矣。
又。
張　勲。
馬上中八箭，步下中四箭。
translation_en:
…with the heart of King Wu, one may punish the cruel and rescue those drowning in distress, without forfeiting a radiance like that of the sun and moon. Without this heart, if one gives free rein to schemes for exhausting military force and waging reckless war, one merely replaces disorder with disorder. How is this any better than the brutality of Jie and Zhou?

Thus, attacking Yuan demonstrated trustworthiness, and the great military review demonstrated ritual propriety; it was said that young and old alike could be employed. Yet these were put into practice through the examples of giving a clod and watching nakedness [?]. And the man who would not capture those with graying hair or beat the drums to attack an enemy whose ranks were not yet formed was nevertheless content with the cruelty of offering a human victim at the altar of the soil [?]. Some even claimed that King Wen’s warfare could not surpass this! How is this different from Robber Zhi’s claiming benevolence and righteousness for dividing the spoils equally and being the last to withdraw?

Thereafter came the violent contention of the seven states, with the people daily ground down; distant attacks upon the four wildernesses daily depleted the state. Alas! Qin and Han were not far removed from the Three Dynasties, yet the tradition of the former kings’ authoritative teachings and proclamations had already grown remote, beyond recovery.

Should military force, then, be abolished altogether? To nurture life without harming it is the intention of the benevolent person; to employ force without brutality is the warfare of a true king. Thus it is said: “Those skilled in governing a state do not raise armies; those skilled in commanding armies do not draw up battle formations; those skilled in deploying formations do not fight.” Those who comprehend this may be addressed concerning the transforming influence that brings order and fulfillment.

Another answer.

Zhang Xun scored eight arrow hits on horseback and four on foot.

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江武舉鄉試錄
text:
大哉聖人正天下之道乎其公物之心與天同
運而濟世之利與天同功何者聖人之道即天
之道也天之道貞觀者也故光明下濟舉萬物
而咸囿於照臨聖人之心與天合一者也故虛
明洞達冐萬物而悉歸於光被是故天運四時
而不宰其功胸肯權刹以時發之而未嘗有所
褻焉聖人奉若天道以行其令也慶賞刑威相
時而動而未嘗尸其化焉然權不可以預設變
===
不可以先圖必炳于未形灼于未著觀陰陽辨
內外察疏親覩強弱燭利害固不先時而失之
遽亦不後時而失之靡不得已而兵與焉凡以
順天應人與天下以廓清之化焉是豈用智自
私拂天道之公而可臻此哉昔者文王念有商
之不德求助予之憂民太公既告之曰王宜修
德下賢惠民以觀天道而復繼之曰大明發而
萬物皆照大兵發而萬物皆服嗟乎其誠達於
punctuated:
大哉，聖人正天下之道乎！其公物之心與天同運，而濟世之利與天同功。何者？聖人之道即天之道也。天之道，貞觀者也，故光明下濟，舉萬物而咸囿於照臨。聖人之心，與天合一者也，故虛明洞達，冐萬物而悉歸於光被。是故天運四時，而不宰其功，胸肯權刹以時發之，而未嘗有所褻焉。聖人奉若天道以行其令也，慶賞刑威，相時而動，而未嘗尸其化焉。然權不可以預設，變不可以先圖，必炳于未形，灼于未著，觀陰陽，辨內外，察疏親，覩強弱，燭利害。固不先時而失之遽，亦不後時而失之靡。不得已而兵與焉，凡以順天應人，與天下以廓清之化焉。是豈用智自私，拂天道之公，而可臻此哉？
昔者文王念有商之不德，求助予之憂民。太公既告之曰：「王宜修德，下賢，惠民，以觀天道。」而復繼之曰：「大明發而萬物皆照，大兵發而萬物皆服。」嗟乎，其誠達於
translation_en:
Great indeed is the Way by which the sage sets the world aright! His impartial concern for all things moves together with Heaven, and the benefits he brings to the world share in Heaven’s achievement. Why is this? The sage’s Way is precisely Heaven’s Way. Heaven’s Way manifests itself with constancy; thus its radiance reaches downward, encompassing all things within its illumination. The sage’s mind is one with Heaven; thus, empty, luminous, and thoroughly discerning, it embraces all things and bathes them in its light. Hence Heaven brings the four seasons round without claiming mastery over their achievements; [the transcription is unclear: 胸肯權刹] brings them forth at the proper time, without ever treating them lightly [?]. The sage follows Heaven’s Way in carrying out his commands. Rewards and punishments are put into effect as the times require, yet he never claims credit for their transforming influence. Expedient measures cannot be laid down beforehand, nor can changing circumstances be planned for in advance. One must perceive clearly what has not yet taken shape and discern what has not yet become apparent: observe yin and yang, distinguish the internal from the external, examine distant and close relationships, assess strength and weakness, and illuminate advantages and dangers. One must neither act before the proper time and err through haste, nor act after it and err through delay. Only when no alternative remains are arms brought into use. All this serves to follow Heaven and respond to the people, bringing the world the transformation of sweeping disorder away. Could anyone attain this by employing cleverness for selfish ends and opposing the impartiality of Heaven’s Way?
Formerly, King Wen reflected on the lack of virtue of the Shang and sought help in his concern for the people [?]. The Grand Duke, Taigong, first told him: “Your Majesty should cultivate virtue, humble yourself before worthy men, and benefit the people, thereby observing Heaven’s Way.” He then added: “When the great light rises, all things are illuminated; when the great army sets forth, all things submit.” Ah! He truly understood …

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江武舉鄉試錄
text:
天人之故者哉夫天道何爲者也一元之氣冲
漠無朕而陰陽以藏其宅四時以奠其位五吏
以宣其化煦嫗相待摩盪相因有無相禪絪緼
化醇太和保合而衆陽之宗照臨晅㬮則莫大
乎日矣故曰大明昔之善言者以彈丸擬其形
以九道律其度以明兩象其離以周天紀其運
以不息徵其恒以容光稽其本葢天之明得日
以章其施而日之光得天以久其照炳炳朗朗
===
晶晶瑩瑩爲雲漢之章爲山川之竅爲草木之
賁舉四海八埏之廣形色倫類之繁孰有能外
於大明者哉乃若聖人則以天自處者也握其
機而設神道之教達其變而鼓不倦之宜隆其
施而運屈伸之感其御世也未嘗不欲居安履
常與天下相忘於無事而置兵革於不試也然
勢激於所趨變生於不測則不得已而制兵焉
故曰天生五材民並用之誰能去兵夫兵凶器
punctuated:
天人之故者哉！夫天道何爲者也？一元之氣，冲漠無朕，而陰陽以藏其宅，四時以奠其位，五吏以宣其化。煦嫗相待，摩盪相因，有無相禪，絪緼化醇，太和保合，而衆陽之宗，照臨晅㬮，則莫大乎日矣，故曰大明。昔之善言者，以彈丸擬其形，以九道律其度，以明兩象其離，以周天紀其運，以不息徵其恒，以容光稽其本。葢天之明得日以章其施，而日之光得天以久其照。炳炳朗朗，晶晶瑩瑩，爲雲漢之章，爲山川之竅，爲草木之賁。舉四海八埏之廣，形色倫類之繁，孰有能外於大明者哉？
乃若聖人，則以天自處者也。握其機而設神道之教，達其變而鼓不倦之宜，隆其施而運屈伸之感。其御世也，未嘗不欲居安履常，與天下相忘於無事，而置兵革於不試也。然勢激於所趨，變生於不測，則不得已而制兵焉。故曰：「天生五材，民並用之，誰能去兵？」夫兵，凶器
translation_en:
…the workings of Heaven and humanity—how truly he understood them! What, then, does the Way of Heaven do? The primal vital force is vast and still, without discernible trace. Within it, yin and yang have their dwelling, the four seasons establish their positions, and the five officers of the elements spread its transforming influence. Warming and nurturing depend on one another; friction and agitation arise from one another. Being and nonbeing alternate; intermingling vital forces bring transformation to fullness, and supreme harmony is preserved in union. As the progenitor of all yang forces, shining down and illuminating [?], nothing is greater than the sun. Hence it is called the Great Brightness. Those of old who spoke well of it likened its shape to a pellet, measured its course by the nine paths, represented its correspondence to the trigram Li through doubled brightness, recorded its movement through the circuit of Heaven, verified its constancy through its ceaseless motion, and investigated its fundamental nature through its penetration of every opening that admits light. Heaven’s brightness obtains the sun to manifest its beneficent action; the sun’s radiance obtains Heaven to sustain its illumination. Brilliant and clear, sparkling and luminous, it gives the River of Heaven its splendor, brings light to the recesses of mountains and rivers, and adorns grasses and trees. Throughout the breadth of the Four Seas and the eight extremities, amid the profusion of forms, colors, orders, and kinds, what can lie outside the Great Brightness?
As for the sage, he takes Heaven as his own model. Grasping its workings, he establishes instruction through the divine Way; comprehending its changes, he promotes tireless, fitting action; magnifying its beneficence, he sets in motion the mutual responses of contraction and expansion. In governing the world, he has always wished to dwell in security and follow the constant order, to live with all under Heaven in such untroubled ease that each forgets the other, and to leave arms and armor unused. Yet when circumstances are driven to extremes by their own momentum, and changes arise unexpectedly, he has no choice but to make provision for warfare. Thus it is said: “Heaven produces the five materials, and the people use them all. Who can dispense with arms?” Now arms are instruments of ill omen…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江武舉鄉試錄
text:
也而有所不能去者聖人經世之慮也以靜待
躁以治待亂有所不輕動者聖人御物之權也
吾嘗徵諸易矣衆正之制於師見之弧矢之利
於睽取之上有六五柔中之大人下應九二陽
德之君子而猶拳拳焉以貞凶悔亡爲戒若是
乎兵之不輕發也今夫日之明於晝也自其懸
車斂耀入虞泉之池曙於蒙谷之浦舒徐泰蒙
泰平之間而後賓於暘谷斯日之所以爲大明
===
而照之所爲不匱也嗟乎聖人之兵以德爲威
而以道用神者也豈非與大明同其朗耀者哉
彼兵家者流其操術非不淵然深矣其設筴非
不較然詳矣然皆智謀機械之末不可與論大
兵之畧也故萬弩齊彀千牛俱奔兵之譎者也
曳柴揚塵誘樵覆絞兵之詐者也毀車崇卒前
偏後伍兵之變者也是皆不聞大兵之義者也
惟王者之兵則有出於軍旅車革之先紀律智
punctuated:
也，而有所不能去者，聖人經世之慮也。以靜待躁，以治待亂，有所不輕動者，聖人御物之權也。吾嘗徵諸《易》矣：衆正之制，於師見之；弧矢之利，於睽取之。上有六五柔中之大人，下應九二陽德之君子，而猶拳拳焉，以「貞凶悔亡」爲戒。若是乎，兵之不輕發也！今夫日之明於晝也，自其懸車斂耀，入虞泉之池，曙於蒙谷之浦，舒徐泰蒙泰平之間，而後賓於暘谷，斯日之所以爲大明，而照之所爲不匱也。
嗟乎！聖人之兵，以德爲威，而以道用神者也，豈非與大明同其朗耀者哉？彼兵家者流，其操術非不淵然深矣，其設筴非不較然詳矣，然皆智謀機械之末，不可與論大兵之畧也。故萬弩齊彀，千牛俱奔，兵之譎者也；曳柴揚塵，誘樵覆絞，兵之詐者也；毀車崇卒，前偏後伍，兵之變者也。是皆不聞大兵之義者也。惟王者之兵，則有出於軍旅車革之先、紀律智
translation_en:
…yet that weapons cannot altogether be dispensed with reflects the sage’s concern for ordering the world. To meet agitation with stillness and disorder with order, refraining from rash action: this is the sage’s discretion in managing affairs. I have sought confirmation of this in the Book of Changes. The ordering of the multitude in rectitude is seen in the hexagram Shi, “The Army”; the advantages of bows and arrows are drawn from Kui, “Opposition.” Above stands the great man of the yielding, central six in the fifth place; below, answering him, is the gentleman possessing the yang virtue of nine in the second place. Yet even then there is earnest insistence upon the warning, “Persistence brings misfortune; regret vanishes.” Such is the care with which arms must be taken up! Consider how the sun shines by day: it halts its carriage and gathers in its radiance, enters the pool of Yuquan, dawns upon the banks of Menggu, and moves gently between Taimeng and Taiping [?], before being received at Yanggu. This is how the sun becomes the great luminary, and how its illumination remains inexhaustible.
Ah! The sage’s use of arms takes virtue as its awe-inspiring power and employs numinous efficacy through the Way. Does it not share the great luminary’s radiance? As for the military specialists, their techniques are certainly profound and their plans certainly precise and detailed. Yet these are all mere subordinate matters of cunning, schemes, and contrivances; such men cannot be engaged in discussing the strategy of the great army. Ten thousand crossbows drawn together and a thousand oxen charging at once are military tricks. Dragging brushwood to raise dust, and using woodcutters as bait to defeat Jiao, are military deceptions. Dismantling chariots to augment the infantry, with chariot units in front and squads of foot soldiers behind, are military adaptations. All these reveal ignorance of the principles of the great army. Only the army of a true king possesses something that precedes troops, chariots, and armor, and rises above discipline and strategic intelligence …

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江武舉鄉試錄
text:
衍之上者矣故其未發而未始有所伺之也既
發而未始有所意之也感發之端迫於天下之
弗若而清明之化溥於天下之相忘以言其兵
之加於天下也十八不能為寡億兆不能為多
而衆弗克與也背固前險無所於圉去國越境
無所於絕而地弗能限也非脅而從之其陣可
壞非利而離之其將可取非弊而勞之其軍可
敗而衍弗足議也聖人之威神於不用而王師
===
之烈彰於不戰是所謂以不用而為用也以不
戰而先屈也其不戰者常在我而必戰者在敵
其不可勝者常在我而可勝者在敵非故養之
使强而罔彼於必折也益之使張而愚彼於必
缺也自其有必戰之罪而不得以遂吾不欲戰
之心則秉其有可勝之釁而後不容弛吾不可
勝之氣其制彌遠其禦無疆藏於九地之下動
於九天之上而形勢在我誠若决積水於萬丈
punctuated: 衍之上者矣。故其未發，而未始有所伺之也；既發，而未始有所意之也。感發之端，迫於天下之弗若；而清明之化，溥於天下之相忘。以言其兵之加於天下也，十八不能為寡，億兆不能為多，而衆弗克與也。背固前險，無所於圉；去國越境，無所於絕，而地弗能限也。非脅而從之，其陣可壞；非利而離之，其將可取；非弊而勞之，其軍可敗，而衍弗足議也。聖人之威，神於不用；而王師之烈，彰於不戰。是所謂以不用而為用也，以不戰而先屈也。其不戰者常在我，而必戰者在敵；其不可勝者常在我，而可勝者在敵。非故養之使强，而罔彼於必折也；益之使張，而愚彼於必缺也。自其有必戰之罪，而不得以遂吾不欲戰之心，則秉其有可勝之釁，而後不容弛吾不可勝之氣。其制彌遠，其禦無疆，藏於九地之下，動於九天之上，而形勢在我，誠若决積水於萬丈
translation_en: …above stratagems [?]. Thus, before such force is deployed, there is nothing by which to watch for it; once deployed, there is nothing by which to anticipate it. What prompts its action is the world’s failure to submit to the right order; yet its clear and enlightened transforming influence spreads throughout the world until people forget its workings. As for the application of its arms throughout the world, eighteen cannot be considered few, nor hundreds of millions many: numerical strength cannot contend with it. With solid defenses behind and dangerous terrain ahead, nothing can hold it back; leaving its own state and crossing borders, nothing can cut it off. Terrain cannot confine it. Without intimidating the enemy into submission, their formations can be broken; without using profit to divide them, their commanders can be captured; without wearing them down through exhaustion, their armies can be defeated. Stratagems [?] are therefore insufficient to explain it. The sage’s awe-inspiring power displays its spiritual efficacy without being employed, and the royal army’s achievements become manifest without battle. This is what is meant by achieving use through non-use, and securing submission in advance without fighting. The capacity to refrain from battle always rests with us; the necessity for battle rests with the enemy. Invincibility always rests with us; vulnerability to defeat rests with the enemy. We do not deliberately nurture them into strength in order to entrap them in certain destruction, or augment their power until they expand in order to delude them into inevitable loss. Only when their offenses make battle necessary, preventing us from fulfilling our desire not to fight, do we seize upon the vulnerabilities that make them defeatable; then we cannot permit our own invincible resolve to slacken. Our control reaches ever farther, and our command knows no bounds. Concealed beneath the nine depths of the earth, moving above the nine heights of heaven, we hold the advantage of position and circumstances. It is truly like releasing accumulated water from a height of ten thousand zhang …

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江武舉鄉試錄
text:
之谿轉圓石於千仞之山其誰得而當之哉故
曰大蓋天下然後能容天下信蓋天下然後能
約天下斯之謂天下之大兵也而王者有獨見
獨聞之德見陰陽而知其心見外內而知其意
見踈親而知其情見强弱而知其形見利害而
知其勢是謂大智不智大謀不謀大勇不勇無
甲兵而勝也無衝機而攻也無溝塹而守也斯
時也大明中天煥乎其章昭乎其輝而祲氛廓
===
清霾曀消鑠魑魅陰邪之迹飄蕩而無遺矣雖
然聖人曷嘗有利天下之心哉吾嘗考文王之
世紂惡已稔毒痡四海極矣而文王方且堅包
瓜之節懋緝熙之敬乃其顯於西土光於四方
則已如日之升矣夫豈待武王牧野之師而後
可見哉太公之言蓋誠有得於斯矣故夫時之
至也聖人不能却其來而勢之積也聖人不能
保其往其與時偕行也即與天合一矣易曰先
punctuated:
之谿，轉圓石於千仞之山，其誰得而當之哉？故曰：「大蓋天下，然後能容天下；信蓋天下，然後能約天下。」斯之謂天下之大兵也。而王者有獨見獨聞之德，見陰陽而知其心，見外內而知其意，見踈親而知其情，見强弱而知其形，見利害而知其勢。是謂大智不智，大謀不謀，大勇不勇，無甲兵而勝也，無衝機而攻也，無溝塹而守也。斯時也，大明中天，煥乎其章，昭乎其輝，而祲氛廓清，霾曀消鑠，魑魅陰邪之迹飄蕩而無遺矣。
雖然，聖人曷嘗有利天下之心哉？吾嘗考文王之世，紂惡已稔，毒痡四海極矣，而文王方且堅包瓜之節，懋緝熙之敬，乃其顯於西土，光於四方，則已如日之升矣。夫豈待武王牧野之師而後可見哉？太公之言，蓋誠有得於斯矣。故夫時之至也，聖人不能却其來；而勢之積也，聖人不能保其往。其與時偕行也，即與天合一矣。《易》曰：「先
translation_en:
… into a ravine, or rolling a round stone down a mountain a thousand ren high—who could withstand it? Thus it is said: “Only when one’s greatness encompasses all under Heaven can one embrace all under Heaven; only when one’s trustworthiness encompasses all under Heaven can one bind all under Heaven together.” This is what is called the supreme military power of all under Heaven. The true king possesses the virtue of seeing and hearing what others cannot. Observing the hidden and the manifest, he knows people’s hearts; observing what is outward and inward, he knows their intentions; observing distant and close relationships, he knows their feelings; observing strength and weakness, he knows their dispositions; observing advantage and harm, he knows the configuration of power. This is called supreme wisdom that does not act clever, supreme planning that does not scheme, and supreme courage that does not display bravery: winning without armor or weapons, attacking without battering engines, and defending without ditches or moats. At such a time, the great luminary stands at the zenith, resplendent in its pattern and brilliant in its radiance. Ominous vapors are swept away, dust haze and darkness dissolve, and every trace of demons and sinister evil is scattered without remainder.
Even so, when did the sage ever harbor a desire to profit from all under Heaven? I have examined the age of King Wen: Zhou’s wickedness had already ripened, and the suffering he inflicted throughout the Four Seas had reached its utmost extent. Yet King Wen still steadfastly maintained the restraint symbolized by “wrapping the melon” and diligently cultivated the reverence of continuous illumination. His manifestation in the western lands and his radiance throughout the four quarters were already like the rising sun. How could it have been necessary to await King Wu’s campaign at Muye before this became apparent? The words of Taigong surely reflect a genuine understanding of this. Thus, when the time arrives, the sage cannot turn back its coming; when circumstances gather force, the sage cannot ensure their passing. To move together with the times is to become one with Heaven. The Book of Changes says: “Before …

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江武舉鄉試錄
text: 天而天弗違後天而奉天時其文武之謂乎
punctuated: 天而天弗違，後天而奉天時。」其文武之謂乎？
translation_en: …Heaven, yet Heaven does not oppose him; following Heaven, he accords with Heaven’s seasons.” Does this not describe Kings Wen and Wu?

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江武舉鄉試錄
text:
浙江武舉鄉試錄後序
嘉靖辛酉冬十月期當貢武
士于京師
侍御崔公如
制舉行式徵諸執事具官以從
度靡不恪所舉士彬彬乎備
材官之良巳存德獲以職事
===
與觀厥成當序諸末序曰古
稱智勇之士抱藝而居莫不
急於自見惟知遇之難耳既
遇矣而出奇决策爲國紓難
或抗辭以邀千乘之主或談
笑以郤百萬之師惟所欲爲
無不輙效萬一事當其難則
punctuated:
浙江武舉鄉試錄後序

嘉靖辛酉冬十月，期當貢武士于京師。侍御崔公如制舉行，式徵諸執事，具官以從，度靡不恪。所舉士彬彬乎備材官之良巳。存德獲以職事與觀厥成，當序諸末。序曰：古稱智勇之士，抱藝而居，莫不急於自見，惟知遇之難耳。既遇矣，而出奇决策，爲國紓難，或抗辭以邀千乘之主，或談笑以郤百萬之師，惟所欲爲，無不輙效。萬一事當其難，則
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Zhejiang Military Provincial Examination

In winter, in the tenth month of the xinyou year of Jiajing [1561], the appointed time arrived to send military candidates to the capital. Censor Cui conducted the proceedings according to the prescribed regulations, duly summoning the officials responsible. The assembled officials followed his direction, observing every rule with care. The men selected displayed an admirable combination of accomplishments, fully possessing the qualities of fine military personnel. I, Cunde, was able, through my official duties, to take part in witnessing the successful completion of these proceedings, and should therefore append a postface. It reads:

Those whom antiquity called men of wisdom and courage lived in possession of their skills, all eager to make themselves known; their sole difficulty was finding someone who recognized and appreciated them. Once they had found such recognition, they devised extraordinary stratagems and settled plans to relieve the state's troubles. Some spoke boldly to win over a ruler of a thousand chariots; others, amid conversation and laughter, repelled an army of a million. Whatever they wished to accomplish invariably proved effective. title: 嘉靖四十年浙江武舉鄉試錄
text:
以狥國爲榮保軀爲辱毅然
祀難正志其聲施皆可被於
後世傳稱國士焉其究知道
者鮮一或動於意氣皆能使
之决性命以就然然諾豈嘗屈
首受書講求大義曉然知其
當爲而爲之者耶爾諸子生
===
長
右文之世涵濡於詩書禮樂之
澤雖誦法管樂祖述孫吴而
其立言多所進退葢皆貴王
賤霸先仁義後功術颯颯乎
立德之敎則非學焉其孰能
辯析之兹旣應格而進御史
punctuated: 以狥國爲榮，保軀爲辱，毅然祀難正志，其聲施皆可被於後世，傳稱國士焉。其究知道者鮮，一或動於意氣，皆能使之决性命以就然然諾，豈嘗屈首受書，講求大義，曉然知其當爲而爲之者耶？爾諸子生長右文之世，涵濡於詩書禮樂之澤，雖誦法管樂，祖述孫吴，而其立言多所進退，葢皆貴王賤霸，先仁義後功術，颯颯乎立德之敎，則非學焉，其孰能辯析之？兹旣應格而進，御史
translation_en:
…they regard dying for the state as an honor and preserving their own bodies as a disgrace, resolutely sacrificing themselves amid danger to affirm their resolve [?]. Their renown can reach later generations, and they are remembered as outstanding men of the realm. Yet few among them thoroughly understand the Way. Once stirred by spirit and ardor, they can all be brought to stake their lives to fulfill a promise [?]. But have they ever bowed their heads to receive instruction, investigated the great principles of righteousness, and acted with a clear understanding that this was what they ought to do?

You gentlemen were born and raised in an age that esteems letters, steeped in the beneficent influence of the Odes, Documents, rites, and music. Although you recite and emulate Guan Zhong and Yue Yi and follow the teachings of Sun Wu and Wu Qi, your writings show considerable discrimination in what they endorse and reject. You esteem the way of the true king above that of the hegemon, placing benevolence and righteousness before achievement and stratagem. Your words vigorously convey the teaching of establishing moral virtue. Without learning, who could make these distinctions? Now that you have met the prescribed standards and advanced, the Censor …

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江武舉鄉試錄
text:
將上其賢而升諸大司馬所
謂處囊之日其末可立見矣
乃若出而謀人之軍制其成
敗其忠智果足以重國而輕
於自視其身否也
朝廷設科以待腹心之將固惟
沉機養畧爲能恢弘仁義之
===
猷以靜其邦家者賢之而吾
顧責以匹夫之所挾以求快
於一逞豈非夫子所謂不與
者與誠嘆之也夫士未有重
視其軀而能果於狥國亦未
有不果於狥國而可以敵愾
於天下者耳俗自治平以來
punctuated:
將上其賢而升諸大司馬，所謂處囊之日，其末可立見矣。乃若出而謀人之軍，制其成敗，其忠智果足以重國而輕於自視其身否也？
朝廷設科以待腹心之將，固惟沉機養畧，爲能恢弘仁義之猷，以靜其邦家者賢之。而吾顧責以匹夫之所挾，以求快於一逞，豈非夫子所謂不與者與？誠嘆之也！夫士未有重視其軀而能果於狥國，亦未有不果於狥國而可以敵愾於天下者耳。俗自治平以來，
translation_en:
…will report their worth and recommend them to the Minister of War. As the saying goes, once an awl is placed in a bag, its point can immediately be seen. Yet when they go forth to plan another’s military operations and determine victory or defeat, will their loyalty and wisdom truly suffice for them to place weight upon the state and regard their own lives lightly?
The court has established this examination to obtain generals whom it can trust as its own confidants. It esteems precisely those who ponder their plans deeply and cultivate strategic judgment, who can broaden the designs of benevolence and righteousness and thereby bring peace to the realm. Yet if I were instead to demand of them the mere courage of an ordinary fellow, seeking gratification in a single reckless exploit, would they not be just those with whom the Master said he would not associate? Truly, this is cause for lament! No man who prizes his own body has ever been resolute in sacrificing himself for his country; nor has anyone lacking that resolve ever been able to oppose the realm’s enemies with righteous ardor. As for prevailing customs, ever since peace and good order were established…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江武舉鄉試錄
text:
恬嬉成習士大夫貴養安矣
於甲胄之士無譏焉何其學
道先乎古人而節信反不逮
之非學之罪學道而二之者
之罪也學貴於一二則惑功
利悅而遷矣二三子其知夫
射乎射之有鵠以一志也明
乎其節之志而不失其事則
功成而德行立是以君子貴
之
===
制以射侯之禮致衆而論士蓋
周制歲貢士於天子而試之
射宮之義其鵠也以其爲臣
委質無二則臣之共吾懼夫
punctuated:
恬嬉成習，士大夫貴養安矣，於甲胄之士無譏焉。何其學道先乎古人，而節信反不逮之？非學之罪，學道而二之者之罪也。學貴於一，二則惑，功利悅而遷矣。二三子，其知夫射乎？射之有鵠，以一志也。明乎其節之志，而不失其事，則功成而德行立，是以君子貴之。

制以射侯之禮致衆而論士，蓋周制歲貢士於天子，而試之射宮之義。其鵠也，以其爲臣委質無二，則臣之共。吾懼夫
translation_en:
…complacency and idle pleasure have become habitual. Scholar-officials prize a life of ease, yet voice no criticism of men in armor. How is it that they surpass the ancients in studying the Way, yet fall short of them in integrity and trustworthiness? This is no fault of learning; the fault lies with those who study the Way with divided commitments. Learning prizes singleness of purpose. Division brings confusion: one delights in profit and advantage and is led astray. You gentlemen, do you understand archery? Archery has a bull’s-eye to concentrate the will. If one understands the intent of its prescribed forms [?] and does not neglect its practice, accomplishment follows and virtuous conduct is established. This is why the gentleman values it.

The established system gathers the multitude and assesses men through the rite of shooting at a target. This embodies the meaning of the Zhou institution whereby men were presented annually to the Son of Heaven and tested in the archery hall. Its bull’s-eye signifies that, as subjects, they pledge their allegiance without divided loyalty: this is the reverence owed by a subject. I fear that…

title: 嘉靖四十年浙江武舉鄉試錄
text:
盡志於射而失其鵠者多矣
夫子之觀於矍相非務武也
而奔軍之將亡國之大夫首
不與焉旣而曰好學不倦好
禮不變耄期稱道而不亂者
在此位豈非先責以爲臣之
禮而後與其至道耶二三子
===
旣以射舉矣愼毋若買櫝者
然忘其珠而徒羨其華美則
市之人羣榰而訾其愚也巳
浙江等處提刑按察司副使
劉存德謹序
punctuated:
盡志於射而失其鵠者多矣。夫子之觀於矍相，非務武也，而奔軍之將、亡國之大夫首不與焉。旣而曰：「好學不倦，好禮不變，耄期稱道而不亂者，在此位。」豈非先責以爲臣之禮，而後與其至道耶？二三子旣以射舉矣，愼毋若買櫝者然，忘其珠而徒羨其華美，則市之人羣榰而訾其愚也巳。
浙江等處提刑按察司副使劉存德謹序。
translation_en:
…many devote their whole attention to archery yet miss its true target. When the Master observed the archery at Juexiang, his purpose was not the pursuit of martial prowess: generals whose armies had fled and grand masters whose states had perished were the first to be excluded. He then said: “Those who love learning without tiring, love ritual without wavering, and, even at eighty or a hundred, expound the Way without confusion—take your places here.” Was this not first to require of them the ritual propriety of a minister, and only afterward to admit them to the highest Way? You gentlemen have now been selected through archery. Take care not to resemble the man who bought the casket, forgetting its pearl and admiring only its splendid appearance; otherwise, the people of the marketplace will gather to point at you [?] and mock your folly.
Respectfully composed as a preface by Liu Cunde, Surveillance Vice Commissioner for Zhejiang and Other Places.
